title: Fake patient portal scam can steal your login and infect your PC
summary: MyChart phishing emails mimic real patient portal alerts with fake lab results and malware tricks that target Windows users across the country.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

If you have ever checked a lab result or sent your doctor a message online, you may already know MyChart. It is a widely used patient portal from Epic that hospitals and medical practices use to give patients online access to health information and care teams.

That growing reliance on patient portals caught the attention of Mary M. She recently wrote to us after hearing from her primary care physician, or PCP, and several specialists about moving more of their patient communication online.
"I just got a lot of updates from my PCP and specialist doctors saying they are moving toward this, but they are already compromised!! I think this is a topic for you!"

Mary raised a concern many patients may share as they hear about scams targeting MyChart users. There is an important point to clear up. The warnings reviewed here describe criminals impersonating MyChart through phishing campaigns. They do not report a breach of the MyChart platform itself.
MEDICARE AND SOCIAL SECURITY SCAMS: WARNING SIGNS AND TIPS
MyChart phishing scams use fake medical results and bogus Medicare offers to exploit trust in patient portals and push victims into sharing sensitive information. (Epic Systems Corporation)

Epic has documented scams that copy the MyChart experience to steal login details. One version can also push malware onto Windows computers. Here's how the scam works and how to protect yourself before a fake MyChart alert catches you off guard.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.
Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com
Why the MyChart phishing scam is getting attention now

This one caught my attention because the warnings are coming from several credible sources at nearly the same time. Penn Medicine said on Aug. 26, 2026, that it was seeing a nationwide scam involving emails and text messages made to look like they came from MyChart. Then, on Aug. 28, Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday warned consumers about another MyChart impersonation scam involving a bogus Medicare Kit.

Epic has also detailed two phishing campaigns its security team investigated this summer. Put all of that together, and you can see why I want you to be especially careful with unexpected MyChart messages right now.

The tricky part is that many of us are already used to getting legitimate emails about appointments or new test results. A fake MyChart alert can land right alongside the real ones, and scammers are counting on you reacting before you take a closer look.
How the fake MyChart results scam works
One campaign starts with a message that looks routine. Epic says the email carries MyChart branding and tells the recipient, "Your recent results are ready."
The button inside the email leads to a fake sign-in page. According to Epic, scammers copied code from the real MyChart site, which helps the page look convincing.
The bogus page asks for an email address and password. If you enter them, the scammers can capture those credentials. Then the attack gets more aggressive.
Fake medical results create panic
After the victim signs in, the fake site displays a made-up medical record. Epic says one version shows a pop-up claiming an "AI-powered review" found critical patterns in blood work.
That is a powerful pressure tactic. A warning about your health can be much harder to ignore than an ordinary phishing message.
Epic says real critical results come from your care team rather than a website pop-up. The fake chart then claims you need to complete a human verification step before seeing more information.
The verification step can install malware

This part should stop you immediately. Epic says the site instructs Windows users to press the Windows key and R, paste content from the clipboard and press Enter. Those steps open the Windows Run box and execute a command the website placed on the clipboard. According to Epic, following those instructions installs malware.

Epic also saw an August 2026 version with an "Unlock Full Report & See Diagnosis" button. Clicking it downloaded a Windows file called Full_Analysis_Report.exe. The page then coached the victim through bypassing the computer's security warning. Your medical results should appear inside MyChart. A patient portal should never require you to download a Windows program to reveal a diagnosis.
FAKE PASSWORD-MANAGER ALERTS COULD PUT YOUR VAULT AT RISK
Fake MyChart pages can mimic real patient portals, using alarming medical claims to pressure users into entering passwords or running malicious Windows commands. (iStock)
Another scam promises a free Medicare Health Kit

The second campaign uses a different hook. Epic says scammers sent fake emails telling people they had been selected for a "2026 Medicare Health Kit." Penn Medicine has also warned about messages advertising a free "MyChart Medicare Kit" or "Senior Health Package." MyChart does not run giveaways.

After someone clicks, Epic says the link can pass through unrelated advertising sites before reaching a fake MyChart-branded survey. A countdown clock pushes the victim to move quickly. Eventually, the site says the kit costs $0 but asks for a shipping fee. Before payment, it collects personal information. The final page asks for credit card details. Epic says no kit ships.
Why a fake MyChart message can be so convincing

Patients already expect electronic messages from doctors and hospitals. A real test-result notification may show up on the same day as a fake one. Scammers can copy that familiar routine. They can also use fear to shorten the amount of time you spend checking a message.

If a fake portal hints at a serious health problem, your first instinct may be to find out what happened. That is why opening the portal independently can make such a difference. We recently covered another healthcare scam that uses fake QR codes around medical settings. Those codes can send patients to bogus sites asking for patient portal credentials or Medicare information. The MyChart campaign follows the same basic idea. The scammer borrows trust from a healthcare service you already recognize.
How to stay safe from fake MyChart messages
A few simple steps can help you slow things down before an urgent-looking message leads you to the wrong place.

If an email says a new result is waiting, avoid using the button inside the message. Open the MyChart app directly. You can also use a saved bookmark or start from your healthcare provider's official website. Epic says each healthcare organization can have its own MyChart URL. You can use MyChart.org to find your provider's official portal.

Do not rely on the sender name alone. An email can display "MyChart" while coming from an unrelated address. Look at the full address and compare it with previous legitimate messages from your healthcare provider. If anything feels off, contact your provider through a phone number or website you already trust.

MyChart says it will never tell you to use keyboard shortcuts or run a command to verify, fix or unlock your account. A website asking you to open the Windows Run box should be an immediate warning sign. Close the page.

MyChart supports two-step verification (2FA). The extra check can help protect your account if someone gets your password. Depending on your setup, you can verify your login through a code or an authenticator app. MyChart also supports passkeys, which can reduce your reliance on a reusable password.

Avoid reusing a password from another important account. A password manager can create and store a strong password for you. If a phishing site captures one password, reuse can turn one stolen login into a much larger problem.

The malware part of this scam shows why strong security protection still has a role. Strong antivirus software can help warn you about malicious downloads or suspicious websites. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com.
Keep Windows and your browser updated too. For more ways to recognize suspicious email, see our guide on how to spot and prevent phishing attacks in your inbox.

If a message claims a serious result needs immediate attention, do not let the urgency decide what you click. Open the official MyChart app yourself or call your provider using a number you already trust. Epic specifically warns that real critical results come from your care team rather than a scary website pop-up.

Scammers can make phishing messages more convincing when they already know details such as your phone number, home address, age or family connections. A data removal service can help remove some of that information from people-search sites and data brokers. It will not stop a fake MyChart message from reaching you, but it can give scammers less personal information to work with when they try to make a message feel legitimate. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.
Epic says MyChart does not run giveaways. If an email promises a free Medicare kit or health package under the MyChart name, do not enter personal information or payment details.
FAKE PARTY INVITATION SCAM CAN HIJACK YOUR COMPUTER
Patients should open MyChart directly through the official app or their healthcare provider’s website rather than clicking links in unexpected emails or texts. (iStock)
What to do if you already clicked a fake MyChart link
Your next move depends on what happened after you opened the page.

Close the page. If you did not enter any information, run a command or download a file, avoid interacting with the site any further. Mark the original message as junk or phishing. Do not click an unsubscribe link inside the suspicious message.

Go to MyChart through the official app or your provider's trusted website. Change your password right away. Then review the contact information saved in your account, including your email address and phone number. If anything looks unfamiliar, contact your healthcare organization's MyChart help desk.
Call your bank or card issuer using the number printed on the card. Tell them the card information went to a fraudulent website and ask about replacing the card.

Disconnect the computer from the internet. Have the computer checked before you use it again for sensitive activity. Run a full security scan with strong antivirus software. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com. Then change important passwords from another trusted device if you used those accounts on the affected computer.

Contact your healthcare provider and health insurer. Medical identity theft can create problems beyond a stolen password. Fraudulent activity can end up connected to your health records or insurance. We explain the warning signs and recovery steps in medical identity theft follows you into the doctor's office.
Kurt's key takeaways

What gets me about this scam is how naturally it fits into something many of us already do. Doctors want patients using portals because they make it easier to see results and stay connected with a care team. Scammers know those messages already have our attention. I would keep using MyChart if my doctors rely on it. I would simply change how I respond to unexpected notifications. If an email says an important result is waiting, I would open the app myself rather than letting the email choose where I go. The malware trick also deserves extra attention. A website asking you to open the Windows Run box or ignore a security warning has crossed a very clear line. Close it and verify the message through your provider. The hardest part may be resisting the fear factor. A message about an abnormal medical result can make anyone move quickly. Taking a few extra seconds to open the real app could protect your patient account and your computer.
Have you received a suspicious MyChart message, or are you becoming more cautious about how you open patient portal alerts? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

SILICON STANDOFF: China is racing to build the data centers and energy infrastructure needed to power artificial intelligence, raising concerns that Beijing’s ability to rapidly construct massive projects could help it get closer to America’s commanding lead in the physical infrastructure underpinning the AI race.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during a press conference following a fatal stabbing incident in Times Square near West 42nd Street and Seventh Avenue in Manhattan, New York, on Aug. 31, 2026. (Kyle Mazza/Anadolu via Getty Images)

President Donald Trump delivers remarks at the "Winning the AI Race" AI Summit at the Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium in Washington, D.C., on July 23, 2025. (Getty)

title: Android Motion Assist could ease car sickness on your phone
summary: Google's Motion Assist places animated dots on Pixel screens to combat motion sickness in vehicles, but the Android 17 rollout remains limited.
story: It’s Distracted Driver Awareness Month, and automakers like GM are putting a focus on high-tech solutions to keep drivers safe behind the wheel.
Ever tried to answer a text from the passenger seat and felt your stomach turn before you reached the second line? For people prone to motion sickness, a phone can go from useful to unbearable fast.

Google is now rolling out a great Android tool designed to make that screen easier to tolerate while the vehicle moves. It is called Motion Assist, and it places animated dots around the edges of your screen that react to the motion of the vehicle.

Apple has offered a similar feature, Vehicle Motion Cues, since iOS 18 arrived in 2024. Google began working on its own version around the same time. It originally appeared under the name Motion Cues before Google renamed it Motion Assist. Now some Pixel owners are starting to see the finished feature on phones running Android 17.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.
Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com
SAMSUNG GALAXY Z FOLD8 LINEUP ADDS THREE CHOICES

Google is rolling out Motion Assist, a new Android feature that uses animated screen cues to help reduce motion sickness for passengers using their phones in moving vehicles. (NickyLloyd via Getty Images)
Why looking at your phone can make you feel sick
Your eyes may tell your brain that you are sitting still and staring at a steady screen. Meanwhile, your inner ear can feel the car moving underneath you.
Those mixed signals can trigger motion sickness. The CDC says it can happen when what you see does not match the movement your body feels, which can leave you nauseous or dizzy.
Reading a text or scrolling through your phone can make things worse because your eyes stay focused on a screen that appears still while the car keeps moving.
How Android Motion Assist works
Motion Assist gives your eyes another visual clue. Small shapes appear around the edges of the display while you continue using the app in the middle of the screen.
Your phone uses motion sensors, including its accelerometer and gyroscope, to follow changes in the vehicle. As the car turns or changes speed, the on-screen cues move along with that motion.
The goal is to give your eyes information that lines up more closely with what your body feels. That may reduce the sensory mismatch that can leave you reaching for the window button.

Google's version also gives you control over the look of the cues with options for shape, size, color and opacity. You can also have Motion Assist activate automatically when your phone detects that you are traveling in a moving vehicle.
Android Motion Assist is rolling out slowly

Here is the frustrating part. You may have Android 17 and still come up empty when you look for Motion Assist. So far, the feature has appeared on select Pixel phones running Android 17. This seems to be a staged rollout rather than a single switch flipped for everyone at once.

The feature appears to arrive through Google Play services rather than through a separate Motion Assist app. Google explains that its system services can deliver new features separately from the main Android operating system update. Google has yet to publish a dedicated Motion Assist support page or a complete list of supported Android phones. So, for now, Android 17 alone may still leave you waiting.
12 BIGGEST APPLE WWDC 2026 TAKEAWAYS YOU NEED TO KNOW
Android users may soon get a built-in way to make reading or texting in the car more comfortable with Google’s new Motion Assist feature. (Hispanolistic via Getty Images)
How to turn on Motion Assist on Android
If Motion Assist has reached your Pixel, here is where to look:

Open Settings.Tap your Google profile at the top.Tap All services.Scroll down to Personal & device safety.Tap Motion Assist.Turn on Start in a moving vehicle if you want Motion Assist to activate automatically when your phone detects that you are riding in a moving vehicle.
Open Settings.
Tap your Google profile at the top.
Tap All services.
Scroll down to Personal & device safety.
Tap Motion Assist.
Turn on Start in a moving vehicle if you want Motion Assist to activate automatically when your phone detects that you are riding in a moving vehicle.
You can also add a Motion Assist tile to Quick Settings so you can turn the feature on or off manually.
Motion Assist also lets you customize the color, shape and opacity of the on-screen cues. A Randomization option can automatically vary those settings.

If you do not see Motion Assist, that does not necessarily mean anything is wrong with your phone. Google appears to be rolling out the feature in stages, and it is still missing from some Pixel phones running Android 17.
What to do if Motion Assist is missing

If you do not see Motion Assist on your Pixel, first make sure your phone is up to date. To check for the latest Pixel software, go to Settings > System > Software updates and install any available update.
Then check your Google Play system update. Go to Settings > Security & privacy > System & updates > Google Play system update. Install any available update and restart your phone if prompted.

However, updating your Pixel may not make Motion Assist appear right away. As mentioned above, Google appears to be rolling out the feature gradually. So, if your phone is fully updated and Motion Assist remains missing, you may simply have to wait for Google to enable it on your device.
How to turn on Vehicle Motion Cues on iPhone
If you have an iPhone, Apple already offers its version of the same idea.
Here is how to turn on Vehicle Motion Cues:

Open Settings.Tap Accessibility.Tap Motion.Tap Vehicle Motion Cues.Choose Automatically in Vehicle if you want your iPhone to turn the feature on when it detects that you are riding in a moving vehicle.
Open Settings.
Tap Accessibility.
Tap Motion.
Tap Vehicle Motion Cues.
Choose Automatically in Vehicle if you want your iPhone to turn the feature on when it detects that you are riding in a moving vehicle.
You can also choose On when you want the cues displayed continuously.

Apple lets you customize the pattern and color. You can also change the size or number of dots shown around the screen. Apple says the feature works best when you are seated facing forward. One important safety note: use this as a passenger feature. Apple warns against using Vehicle Motion Cues while operating a moving vehicle.
ANDROID FAKE CALL DETECTION WARNS YOU ABOUT SCAMS
Google’s Motion Assist uses your phone’s motion sensors to display moving dots that may help reduce the sensory mismatch linked to motion sickness. (Baona via Getty Images)
Will moving dots really help motion sickness?

The idea may sound almost too simple, but it targets the sensory conflict linked to motion sickness. Still, everyone responds differently. Apple describes Vehicle Motion Cues as a feature that may help reduce motion sickness. Google uses similar language for Motion Assist.

Think of the moving cues as another tool you can try rather than a guaranteed fix. If the screen still makes you feel sick, put the phone down and look toward the horizon. The CDC includes looking at the horizon among its strategies for reducing motion sickness.
Another option is to listen instead of looking at your phone. We have a step-by-step guide showing how to get your phone to read articles aloud on both iPhone and Android at Cyberguy.com.
Why this Android feature is worth checking
A row of moving dots may sound like a tiny phone feature until you are the person who cannot answer a message from the back seat without feeling queasy.
That is what makes Motion Assist interesting. Google is trying to solve a very ordinary problem using sensors already inside your phone. You need no extra app or accessory.
If the feature works for you, a car ride could become a chance to catch up on messages or read something longer without immediately regretting it.
Kurt's key takeaways

I like phone features that solve an annoyance you feel in everyday life. Motion Assist falls squarely into that category. If you get motion sickness, I would try the automatic setting as soon as it appears on your Pixel. There is very little effort involved, and you will know quickly whether the moving cues help you. iPhone owners already have a similar option hiding in Accessibility. That is also a good reminder to explore those settings from time to time. Some of the most useful features on your phone can sit there unnoticed for months.
Would moving dots on your screen make you more willing to use your phone during a car ride, or would you rather put the phone away completely? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

title: The privacy risk of moving to a retirement community
summary: Moving to a 55+ community can quickly expose your data to scammers and data brokers before you even unpack, putting your whole family at risk.
story: Artificial intelligence is rapidly accelerating elder fraud schemes across the U.S., targeting older Americans who hold a significant share of household wealth. ScamSkeptic founder Matt Sanner joins 'America's Newsroom' to highlight how fraudsters utilize AI to mimic voices and create deepfakes. Sanner provides key strategies for families to identify these scams and protect their vulnerable loved ones.

The moving truck hasn't even left the driveway. Somewhere, a scammer may already know three things about you: your name, your new address and something about your age. Maybe not your exact age, but potentially enough information to make you a more attractive target.

Federal law sets specific rules for communities that qualify as housing for people 55 and older. One requirement says at least 80% of occupied units must house at least one person who is 55 or older. Those requirements come from the Housing for Older Persons Act.

That means an address inside a known 55+ community can give scammers and data brokers another clue about you. Once public records connect your name to that address, data brokers can add it to a much larger profile.

That is the part nobody mentions in the moving checklist. Here is how that profile can come together so quickly. More importantly, here is how you can reduce the personal information scammers can find.
FIVE DATA BROKER OPT-OUT MYTHS THAT LEAVE RETIREES EXPOSED
Scammers can combine property records, people-search listings and community information to build convincing profiles of new retirement community residents. (Getty Images)
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.

How moving to a 55+ community can expose your data
Moving into an age-restricted community does more than change your ZIP Code. It can quickly create a new, highly concentrated data profile.
Here's what can become available:

Your name and new address can appear in county property records after officials file the deed. Anyone can then search that information.Your HOA gets your contact information. Some communities also distribute resident directories with names, addresses and phone numbers.New-mover marketing companies identify people who recently relocated. They can then sell those details to advertisers.People-search sites such as Spokeo and Whitepages may update listings with your new address, age range and household details.Community Facebook groups, welcome committees and bulletin boards sometimes post new-neighbor introductions. Those posts may include names, photos or unit numbers.
Your name and new address can appear in county property records after officials file the deed. Anyone can then search that information.
Your HOA gets your contact information. Some communities also distribute resident directories with names, addresses and phone numbers.
New-mover marketing companies identify people who recently relocated. They can then sell those details to advertisers.
People-search sites such as Spokeo and Whitepages may update listings with your new address, age range and household details.
Community Facebook groups, welcome committees and bulletin boards sometimes post new-neighbor introductions. Those posts may include names, photos or unit numbers.
Each detail may seem harmless by itself. However, scammers can combine those details to build a convincing profile of you.
SELLING YOUR HOME? YOUR DATA IS ALREADY MOVING
Privacy experts recommend checking what information appears online, limiting community directory listings and requesting removal from data broker sites. (Getty Images)
Research shows scams can start soon after a move

Criminologists at Florida State University spent years studying financial exploitation inside a large Florida retirement community. Their findings should change how you think about your first few months in a new home. Residents told researchers that scammers targeted them immediately and repeatedly after they moved into the retirement community. They also faced scams far more often than before their move.

One of the study's authors, Julie Brancale, told AARP that residents faced targeting almost immediately after moving in. She said the attempts then continued. Her colleague, Thomas Blomberg, described another problem. People may move into gated communities expecting greater safety during retirement. Instead, they can face repeated scam attempts.

AARP's reporting on The Villages also highlights real cases of financial exploitation. The Villages is the country's largest 55+ community and has more than 150,000 residents. For example, a pair posing as pool contractors allegedly collected nearly $200,000 in down payments from six residents. Police later arrested them. A Leisure World resident in Maryland lost close to $800,000 in a gold-bar scam. Meanwhile, one local anti-fraud group estimates that it has recovered roughly $40 million for Florida victims over the years.
How retirement community scams can target your family

Here's the part that should get your attention. When a scammer searches for information about you, your adult children may appear too. Data broker profiles may list them as relatives and connect them to current addresses. As a result, a scam aimed at a new resident can spread to the whole family.

A criminal may never need to trick you directly. For example, someone could call your daughter and pretend to represent your new HOA. The caller could mention your real address and ask her to confirm a payment on your behalf. That request can sound convincing because the caller already knows personal details. The more information criminals collect beforehand, the easier they can make a fake story sound believable.
How big is fraud targeting older Americans?

This problem reaches far beyond individual retirement communities. The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center logged more than 201,000 fraud complaints from Americans 60 and older in 2025. Those complaints totaled more than $7.7 billion in reported losses.

The FTC estimates that the true financial impact could reach as high as $81.5 billion after accounting for unreported cases. An analysis of FBI complaint data also found another troubling link. Roughly 72% of fraud categories affecting older adults can become more dangerous when attackers have access to personal information.
The takeaway is simple. Personal information gives scammers material they can use to make a fraudulent call, text or email sound more believable.
THE ONE THING SCAMMERS CHECK BEFORE TARGETING YOU ONLINE
Moving into a 55+ community can expose your age range, new address and family connections through public records and data broker sites. (iStock)
How to protect your privacy in a retirement community
You cannot prevent every county property record from becoming public. However, you can reduce how much additional information someone finds once they start looking.

First, ask your HOA or community manager whether you can limit or opt out of resident directory listings. Also, ask what information the community shares with other residents. If possible, remove your phone number, email address and photo from community directories.

Next, search your name, phone number and new address online to see what appears. People-search sites and data brokers may already connect your new location with your age range, relatives and previous addresses.
Remove your information from data broker sites

You can submit removal requests directly to people-search sites and data brokers that list your information, but doing it yourself can take a lot of time and effort. A data removal service can handle those requests on your behalf and continue checking whether your information reappears. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.
Kurt's key takeaways

Moving into a 55+ community can create a privacy risk earlier than many people realize. What concerns me most is how quickly your new address can become connected to your age range, relatives and other personal details across public records and data broker sites.

The Florida State University research really stands out to me because residents reported scam attempts soon after moving. To me, that means privacy needs to be part of your moving checklist before you unpack the boxes, not something you think about after suspicious calls start coming in.

I would also pay close attention to what your information reveals about your family. Data broker profiles often connect relatives, previous addresses and household details. That gives scammers more ways to make a fake story sound convincing to you or someone close to you.

With Americans 60 and older reporting more than $7.7 billion in fraud losses to the FBI in 2025, I would not wait for a scam attempt to start protecting your information. Search for your name and address online, ask what your community shares and remove personal data from broker sites wherever possible.

story: Officials reveal a series of indictments and anticipated arrests of Chinese nationals as federal authorities expand enforcement efforts into alleged criminal networks.

Two Chinese nationals were arrested in China after allegedly supplying synthetic drugs that prosecutors say were imported into the United States and later distributed to inmates at federal and state prisons nationwide.

Lisa Xing, 36, and Zhanwen Song, 38, were charged in a superseding federal indictment in the Eastern District of Texas with drug trafficking and money laundering offenses tied to an alleged scheme that allegedly supplied synthetic opioids, cannabinoids and other drugs from China for distribution in U.S. correctional facilities.

FBI Director Kash Patel touted the case in a post on X, writing that the defendants allegedly trafficked "dangerous synthetic drugs from China into the United States — including smuggling them into our prison systems."

According to prosecutors, Xing and Song shipped synthetic drugs to co-defendants Adell Willis of Texas and Judy Ly of Michigan, who allegedly dissolved the drugs into liquid, soaked sheets of paper in the mixture and mailed them to inmates in federal and state prisons across the country.

title: NYPD chief: 9/11 heroes’ legacy lives on in every generation of officers
summary: The NYPD memorial wall at One Police Plaza honors 23 officers killed on 9/11 and hundreds more lost to World Trade Center-related illnesses.
story: Mayor Zohran Mamdani recounts Officer John William Perry’s final act of heroism as he honors the officers killed that morning and those who later died from 9/11-related illnesses as the city unveils a new memorial to their legacy.

The legacy of the NYPD officers who ran toward danger on Sept. 11, 2001, continues to shape the department a quarter-century later, Chief of Department Michael LiPetri said during a ceremony dedicating a memorial wall to members who died in the attacks and their aftermath.
"None of us gets here alone," LiPetri said. "Whatever rank we reach, whatever command we lead, we are standing on the foundations other people built."
"We inherit their lessons, their example, and eventually it becomes our responsibility to pass those things forward," he added.
FOX NEWS MEDIA ANNOUNCES EXTENSIVE 9/11 ANNIVERSARY COVERAGE FROM GROUND ZERO, PENTAGON AND SHANKSVILLE
Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during an unveiling ceremony for a new 9/11 Memorial Wall at One Police Plaza on Sept. 9, 2026, in New York City. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

The NYPD has lost more than 469 members to illnesses connected to their service after the attacks, Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said. More than 1,700 members have retired from the department with World Trade Center-related disabilities, LiPetri added.

"We are still losing members to illnesses caused by their service after the attacks," LiPetri said. "All these years later, we are still standing with families as they bury loved ones whose lives were forever changed by the work they did after Sept. 11."
9/11 VICTIM'S IDENTITY EMERGES NEARLY 25 YEARS LATER AFTER DNA BREAKTHROUGH CRACKS MYSTERY

The memorial wall at One Police Plaza honors the 23 NYPD officers killed at the World Trade Center that morning, along with members who later died from illnesses linked to their rescue and recovery efforts.

"Sept. 11 did not end on Sept. 11," NYPD Chief Chaplain Rev. A.R. Bernard said during the invocation. "For many, the costs continued for years, illness endured, families impacted and lives ultimately lost."
FRANK SILLER: 'I LOVE YOU, BROTHER' -- THE 9/11 LOSS THAT INSPIRED A MISSION OF SERVICE

Mayor Zohran Mamdani recalled the story of Officer John William Perry, who was at One Police Plaza preparing to resign and begin a career as an attorney when the first plane struck the North Tower. Perry asked for his shield back and rushed to the World Trade Center.

"There he was confronted with unimaginable suffering, but he did not stop with the same immense bravery and courage that was commonplace among so many that day, the kind that has long defined this department," Mamdani said.

"Officer Perry ran into the fire. The last time he was seen he was helping a woman out of the South Tower before rushing back in to save as many others as he could. Officer Perry and 22 of his fellow officers, each with their own stories, were killed that morning. That includes 14 members of the emergency service unit, who were among the first to enter the towers."
TRUMP POSTHUMOUSLY AWARDS MEDAL OF FREEDOM TO 9/11'S 'MAN IN RED BANDANA'

The new 9/11 Memorial Wall at One Police Plaza was unveiled Sept. 9, 2026, by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Commissioner Jessica Tisch, family members of first responders and other NYPD officers. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Mamdani noted that the sons of officers Ronnie Klopfer and Joseph Viviano "now carry on his legacy of bravery as valued members of this very department."
"Every officer present that day embodied the NYPD’s creed that the duty to protect is not a job that one clocks out of, but a calling," Mamdani said. "One answers until the very end.

"In the days and months that followed Sept. 11, thousands of NYPD officers and staff from across every precinct and every borough heeded that same call. They took on that same heavy and incalculable risk."

story: Video footage showing the fiery aftermath of a fatal plane crash on Sept. 7, 2026, at the Montgomery-Gibbs Executive Airport.
A deadly airplane crash in San Diego, California, on Monday killed the two people on board.
Video footage shows the fiery aftermath as a plume of thick, black smoke billowed out from the wrecked Cessna at the Montgomery-Gibbs Executive Airport.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) provided preliminary information to Fox News Digital which stated, "A Cessna 172 crashed while landing at Montgomery-Gibbs Executive Airport in California around 5:15 p.m. local time on Monday, Sept. 7. "An NTSB investigator is en route to the scene and is expected to arrive this afternoon," the NTSB's statement first issued Tuesday noted. title: Blue-city police chief draws scrutiny after referring to known gun violence suspects as ‘trigger pullers’
summary: Interim Chief Andre Sayles unveiled a strategy targeting known "trigger pullers" after three deadly Seattle shootings over Labor Day weekend.
story: ‘The Five’ co-hosts discuss deadly gun violence in Seattle over Labor Day weekend and the police department’s response.

Seattle’s interim police chief referred to known gun-violence suspects as "trigger pullers" during a Labor Day weekend news conference where he discussed three separate shootings and his department’s response.
Three people were killed, and three others were injured in the shootings over a 24-hour stretch, FOX 13 Seattle reported.

Interim Chief Andre Sayles said the Seattle Police Department was increasing patrols, coordinating with business owners, and deploying its community response group and gun violence reduction unit to curb the violence.
SEATTLE MAYOR KATIE WILSON NAMES ANDRE SAYLES AS INTERIM POLICE CHIEF AFTER BARNES RESIGNATION

"We’re looking at ways to where we can identify individuals that are known, we call trigger pullers, in our community," Sayles said during a Sept. 7 briefing. "Identifying them, making sure that we’re putting cases on those individuals working with King County Prosecutor’s Office, to bring these individuals to justice, because the families that lost loved ones, throughout the year and years past, deserve justice."
Seattle Police investigate a mass shooting in the city. (KCPQ)
Seattle police told Fox News Digital on Wednesday that "trigger puller" is an informal term and is not required by department policy.
The term drew pushback from local commentators who said it softened the description of violent suspects.
"So in Seattle we aren’t calling them ‘shooters’ anymore? Now they are ‘trigger pullers’?" local radio host Ari Hoffman posted on social media following Sayles’ remarks.
The phrase is not new to law enforcement. In 2022, then-FBI Director Christopher Wray used the term during remarks to the Association of State Criminal Investigative Agencies.

"You all know what’s driving the violent crime in your states," Wray said. "Whether it’s a community where a disproportionate amount of gun violence takes place or rival gangs wreaking havoc in a particular region or a handful of well-known trigger pullers who keep finding their way back to the streets, no matter how many times they’re arrested, at the FBI, we want to be your integral partner in the fight against violent crime."
Seattle police work at the scene of a shooting. (KCPQ)
Sayles said investigators did not believe the three shootings were connected and that none appeared to be linked to the deadly July shooting at the Bite of Seattle festival.

The first shooting occurred early Sunday near Denny Way and Clay Street, where a fight following a street takeover escalated into gunfire, killing a 20-year-old man and injuring two others, FOX 13 Seattle reported.
About an hour later, a gunman fired multiple shots into a vehicle near Third Avenue and Blanchard Street, fatally wounding a 23-year-old woman.

No arrests had been made in the three shootings when Sayles spoke with reporters. He said investigators were working with witnesses and reviewing surveillance footage, including about 450 hours of video in one case.

Mayor Katie Wilson listens to an attendee after a vigil a day after the Bite of Seattle food festival shooting on July 27, 2026. Three people were killed and four wounded. (Getty Images)

title: Accused wife killer Barry Morphew back behind bars after separate incident that skyrocketed bond: prosecutors
summary: Barry Morphew's bond jumped to $10 million cash after prosecutors alleged a hit-and-run incident and argued the accused wife killer is a flight risk.
story: Colin McCallin, a Colorado-based lawyer and former deputy district attorney for the 18th Judicial District Attorney's Office in Colorado, told Fox News Digital that a trial without Suzanne Morphew's body available could create problems.
A judge hiked accused wife killer Barry Morphew's bond to $10 million after he allegedly fled a crash following an airport run to pick up his daughter.

A grand jury indicted Barry Morphew on June 20, 2025, on a charge of first-degree murder after deliberation in connection with the death of his wife, Suzanne Morphew, 49, a mother of two daughters. Suzanne Morphew vanished on Mother's Day 2020 in Colorado, where the couple resided. Barry Morphew was taken into custody in Goodyear, Arizona, nearly 11 hours away from the location where his wife was last seen.

Prosecutors allege that Barry Morphew was involved in a hit-and-run accident on Aug. 26 at 7:30 p.m., when an individual observed him driving "aggressively" before striking two cars. CBS News obtained a video of the driver's interaction with Morphew where he refused to give his name or identification, also indicating he didn't have insurance. He was arrested by Boulder County sheriff's deputies on Sept. 3 and remains behind bars.

Officials said Barry Morphew offered the other driver $300 for damage caused to her car, which she refused. Barry Morphew was seen on video buffing scratches on the other driver's car with a T-shirt and his hand.

At the time, prosecutors said Barry Morphew was picking up his daughter from the airport.

title: Amazon cargo jet pilot reportedly told wife, 'My career is over' shortly after deadly crash
summary: A pilot from the Amazon cargo plane crash at Miami International Airport reportedly told a bystander his career was over after the fiery Boeing 767 wreck.
story: Fox News correspondent Danamarie McNicholl reports on the Miami-Dade sheriff confirming the identities of five victims killed after an Amazon cargo plane overshot the runway at Miami International Airport and struck a van. McNicholl also details the NTSB investigation as officials examine flight data and cockpit voice recorders to determine the cause of the crash on ‘The Story.’

After an Amazon cargo plane crashed at Miami International Airport, killing five people, one of the pilots reportedly told his wife over the phone that his "career was over," according to a new report.
Abraham Altamar told CBS News that he had witnessed the fiery wreck on Sunday while he was working in a nearby building. He did not identify which of the two pilots he spoke with.
Altamar was on FaceTime with his wife when he said the pilot approached him.
"He was, like, shaking and, and a little injured in his forehead and his hand," Altamar said. "I was like, 'Hey, you want me to call 911?' He's like, 'No, we already called them.'"
AMAZON CARGO PLANE OVERRUNS MIAMI AIRPORT RUNWAY AND STRIKES 'MULTIPLE' VEHICLES; 5 DEAD, 5 INJURED

Investigators continue working on Tuesday, Sept. 8, 2026, after an Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767 went through a fence and hit vehicles at Miami International Airport on Sunday. (Al Diaz/Miami Herald/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)
The pilot then called his wife on Altamar's phone to tell her what had happened, CBS reported.
Altamar said the pilot told his wife that he was fine, while instructing her to tell his mother that he was in an accident but survived.
During this conversation, the pilot also reportedly said, "My career is over."
The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office identified the two pilots as Joseph Carroll, 55, and Jaime Felipe Silva Molina, 37.
A police officer looks on at the Amazon cargo plane on Monday, Sept. 7, 2026, after it crashed at Miami International Airport on Sunday. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)
UPS PLANE ABORTS LANDING IN NEAR MISS AT SAME AIRPORT WHERE NOVEMBER CRASH KILLED 15
A LinkedIn profile for Carroll lists him as a captain for 21 Air, the company operating the plane that crashed over the weekend. A profile for Molina lists him as a first officer at 21 Air.
Federal Aviation Administration records show both men hold airline transport pilot certificates and are qualified to fly Boeing 767 aircraft, the model involved in the Miami crash.
The aircraft was on its third flight of the day when it tried landing at Miami International.
Damaged vehicles are seen at Miami International Airport on Monday, Sept. 7, 2026, after an Amazon cargo plane crashed into them on Sunday in Miami, Florida. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)
FRONTIER JET STRIKES, KILLS PERSON ON DENVER AIRPORT RUNWAY DURING TAKEOFF AFTER SECURITY BREACH

The jet overshot the runway by at least 1,300 feet beyond the paved surface before crashing into multiple vehicles, including a 2012 white Ford Econoline van with passengers inside, National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy said during a Monday press conference.
The aircraft then crashed through the airport perimeter and struck a civilian vehicle, a Toyota Corolla Cross LE.
On Tuesday, Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz released the names of the five people who were killed, all of whom were inside vehicles that were hit by the plane.

Jennifer Homendy, chairwoman of the National Transportation Safety Board, holds a press conference on the investigation into the Amazon Cargo plane crash at Miami International Airport on Sept. 7, 2026, in Miami, Florida. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

They were identified as: Rolando Aleman Leon, 55; Yoel Rodriguez Naranjo, 53; Julio C. Pineda, 75; Carlos Acosta Fajardo, 53; and 47-year-old Javierkys Reyes Quevedo.
Five others were injured, including the pilots, who were treated and released. The other three people remained hospitalized as of Tuesday, with two of them in critical condition.

The panel of nine women and three men deadlocked after splitting 11-1, but one woman, identified as Juror No. 5, told local media that the holdout at the end of deliberations wasn't the only one who initially thought Clancy was guilty.
Based on some of their statements, Clancy's defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, told "CBS Mornings" Wednesday that he would file a new motion to dismiss on double jeopardy grounds.

title: Lindsay Clancy attorney's appeal to Trump for pardon could hurt his credibility, expert says
summary: Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney Kevin Reddington made a surprise appeal to Trump for a pardon after the mistrial, but legal experts are skeptical.
story: Attorney Mark Bederow reacts to the unexpected request for a presidential pardon from Lindsay Clancy's attorney Kevin Reddington while breaking down what prosecutors would need to do if they plan to bring the case to trial again.

After Lindsay Clancy's criminal defense attorney made a surprise appeal to President Donald Trump for a pardon Tuesday morning, legal experts dismissed the request as unrealistic while questioning the strategy.

"There isn't going to be a pardon for the simple reason there is no mechanism by law which would allow said pardon," said Mark Bederow, a New York City-based criminal defense attorney who has been following the case.

The 36-year-old former nurse faced three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan. After their deaths, she attempted to kill herself and was paralyzed from the injuries. Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial for Clancy Friday after jurors deadlocked following a full week of deliberations.

"This is a very credible, skilled lawyer, and these comments, I think, lack credibility," Bederow told Fox News Digital. "In some level, they lack seriousness because we know it, it's not going to happen — so I don't see the advantage of giving an interview where the only thing people are talking about is Lindsay Clancy's attorney is seeking a pardon or intervention from the president of the United States in the Massachusetts state case."
TRUMP WEIGHS IN ON LINDSAY CLANCY MURDER TRIAL DUBBED 'KANGAROO COURT' BY GOP LEADERS
Lindsay Clancy sits next to her defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, during her murder trial at Plymouth Superior Court on Aug. 11, 2026. (Jonathan Wiggs/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)

Clancy attorney Kevin Reddington said Clancy's "life was ruined" after she went to an inexperienced doctor who prescribed medications to treat her postpartum depression in an interview on ABC's "Good Morning America" Tuesday. When asked "what's next" for his client, he appealed directly to the president.

"I'd like to say that perhaps Donald Trump, who felt compelled to speak out about this case, may very well — Mr. President, I would hope that you would consider this young lady the type of the person she is, what she's been through, and consider a pardon," he said.
LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL DECLARED AFTER JURY DEADLOCKS IN KILLINGS OF HER THREE CHILDREN
Lindsay Clancy's attorney, Kevin Reddington, speaks outside the courthouse after the third day of deliberations in her murder trial on Aug. 31, 2026. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)

In a separate interview with Massachusetts' WBZ-TV, Reddington said that while he understands Trump has no grounds to issue a pardon on state charges, he felt that the president could potentially influence the case.

"He certainly has an awful lot of clout, and I'm sure that were he hypothetically to reach out to [Plymouth County District Attorney] Tim Cruz, they're both Republicans, I don't know, maybe that would be something that Tim would listen to and consider," he said. "I think any type of help that we can get is helpful."

Kevin Reddington appealed to President Donald Trump regarding Lindsay Clancy's case. (Yuri Gripas/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

title: Data shows Amazon jet’s key braking systems did not deploy during deadly Miami crash: NTSB
summary: The NTSB said the cargo jet’s wheel brakes were applied, but its speed brakes and thrust reversers did not deploy, according to available data.
story: The NTSB said the thrust reversers and speed brakes did not deploy when an Amazon cargo jet overran the runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday, according to available data.

Authorities on Tuesday said key braking systems did not deploy during Sunday’s deadly plane crash after an Amazon cargo jet overran the runway at Miami International Airport and struck two vehicles, killing five people.
While the aircraft’s wheel brakes were applied, available data indicates that the speed brakes and thrust reversers did not, according to the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB).
There was "no indication in the recorded data that speed brakes or thrust reversers were deployed," Chihoon Shin, the NTSB investigator in charge, said.
Shin said investigators plan to interview the pilots involved, adding that officials are not yet going to speculate about what should have happened during the landing.
AMAZON CARGO PLANE OVERRUNS MIAMI AIRPORT RUNWAY AND STRIKES 'MULTIPLE' VEHICLES; 5 DEAD, 5 INJURED

An Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767 crashes off the runway and crushes a vehicle near the Miami International Airport in Miami on Sunday, Sept. 6, 2026. (Al Diaz/Miami Herald/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

"When we analyze the full list of parameters, we'll have a better idea of the aircraft's performance during this landing. Was it normal? Was it not? And what was working and what was not. So I'm not going to speculate on what should have been right now," he said.

"What we need to do is talk to the crew and get their account to understand how they're manipulating the controls in order to get a better understanding of the situation," he added. "That's something that we need a complete understanding of."
VICTIMS IDENTIFIED IN FATAL AMAZON CARGO JET CRASH AT MIAMI AIRPORT
NTSB investigators examine a wreckage field Monday after a Boeing 767 cargo plane overran the end of Runway 30 while landing Sunday at Miami International Airport. (@NTSB_Newsroom/X)

While officials did not identify the pilots involved, NTSB Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy said the captain was 55 years old and had 7,145 flight hours, according to his latest Class 1 medical certificate dated March 31, 2026.
The first officer was 37 years old and had 2,655 flight hours, according to his Class 1 medical certificate dated April 13, 2026, she said.
Officials confirmed that no hazardous materials were on board and said most of the cargo consisted of contact lenses.
An Amazon cargo plane is seen after it crashed at Miami International Airport on Sept. 6, 2026, in Miami, Florida. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

"They did confirm there was no hazmat on board. The cargo was mainly made up of contact lenses, again weighing 32,222 pounds. And then, of course, a flight kit," she said.At least five people were killed, and another five were injured in Sunday’s fiery crash involving Prime Air Flight 7598.

Seven of the victims were in a van that was crushed on airport property. The plane then traveled through the airport fence and struck another civilian vehicle before coming to a stop near a parking lot.

title: Cold case takes grim turn after remains identified as runaway teen; homicide investigation underway
summary: Advanced DNA testing and genetic genealogy identified remains found near a North Carolina manufacturing facility as those of a Maryland teen who vanished in 1977.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Authorities announced a major breakthrough in a decades-old cold case, identifying human remains found nearly 49 years ago in North Carolina as belonging to a runaway 15-year-old girl who disappeared from Maryland.
The skeletal remains were discovered more than six months after Cindy Marcell Blizzard went missing in the spring of 1977, according to the North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation (SBI).

Authorities said the manner of death remained undetermined, but the case was being investigated as a homicide. They said the remains were found in a wooded area near a Wilson County manufacturing facility roughly five hours south of Blizzard's home.
The "circumstances surrounding the location and recovery of the remains raised the probability of foul play, and the investigators are treating the case as a homicide," the SBI said.
TEEN FOUND IN SHALLOW CALIFORNIA VINEYARD GRAVE IDENTIFIED NEARLY 50 YEARS LATER AS FAMILY WARNS KILLER
Authorities identified human remains found nearly 49 years ago as those of Maryland runaway teen Cindy Marcell Blizzard. (North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation )
According to officials, skeletal remains and clothing were found Dec. 29, 1977, near a Firestone plant that produces vehicle tires.
A medical examiner determined the remains had likely been there for six months to two years and belonged to a white female between 16 and 23 years old.
In the decades that followed, the case went cold as forensic technology was not advanced enough to identify the remains, authorities said.
"For years, investigators compared dental records against missing persons cases without finding a match," the SBI said.
GIRL KNOWN AS 'CHELSEA JANE DOE' ID'D 26 YEARS AFTER MUTILATED BODY FOUND HUNDREDS OF MILES FROM HOME STATE

FILE — A road runs through a wooded area in Asheville, North Carolina. Investigators are pursuing a homicide probe in the case of a missing teen whose remains were found in a wooded area.  (George Rose/Getty Images)
The case was reopened in 2010 by a state anthropologist, who submitted the remains for DNA testing and cross-referenced the results with federal databases, officials said.
However, the investigation did not gain momentum until 2024, when the SBI’s Cold Case Investigative Team reviewed the case again using forensic tools that did not exist in 1977.
WOMAN FOUND IN SHALLOW GRAVE ID’D AFTER 44 YEARS AS MILLIONAIRE TIED TO ESTATE MURDER PLOT
When the case qualified for advanced DNA testing, forensic scientists extracted preserved genetic material from a bone sample, according to the authorities.
"A genealogy service used the profile to trace potential relatives, pointing investigators toward a 15-year-old girl who had run away from Monkton, Maryland, in the spring of 1977," the SBI said.

The identification was made with assistance from the FBI’s NCIC Investigation and Operational Assistance Group, the Maryland Department of State Police Homicide Unit and the Raleigh Police Department’s Intel Unit, authorities said.
FILE — A young doctor conducts research in a laboratory. Forensic teams in North Carolina have identified the skeletal remains found nearly 49 years ago in Wilson County.  (iStock)

title: Judge orders Alex Murdaugh murder retrial moved to nearby county
summary: Alex Murdaugh's double murder retrial moves to Sumter County after a judge ruled Colleton County's jury pool was too compromised for a fair trial.
story: During court testimony, witness Phil Barber refutes claims regarding a lack of affordable lodging near the Charleston County Courthouse. He also addresses parking accessibility and notes that weekend hotel price increases would not impact weekday court proceedings.
A South Carolina judge on Tuesday granted a request by Alex Murdaugh that the double-murder retrial for the disgraced attorney be relocated to a new venue.
Judge Debra McCaslin ruled that the trial will take place in Sumter County. Defense lawyers argued that Colleton County's jury pool was tainted by the highly covered original trial.

In her order, McCaslin wrote that Murdaugh can receive a fair trial in Sumter County, adding that it offers adequate security measures, courtroom facilities, and technological capabilities to conduct proceedings.

"The judge considered several factors including the financial impact on Colleton County, the convenience of witnesses, courthouse security, transportation and security of Murdaugh, courtroom facilities, and technological capabilities," the order states.
Murdaugh's attorneys had suggested Charleston or Richland County courthouses for the venue transfer before McCaslin made her ruling.
ALEX MURDAUGH RETURNS TO COURT AS DEFENSE ARGUES FOR RETRIAL MOVE AFTER CLERK SCANDAL POISONED JURY POOL
Fox News Digital has reached out to Murdaugh's attorneys and prosecutors.

As a result, the court unanimously overturned his 2023 convictions and two life sentences.
Murdaugh is charged with murder and weapons offenses for the June 2021 shooting deaths of his wife, Maggie, and 22-year-old son, Paul, at their family estate.

title: Lindsay Clancy juror admitted 'reasonable doubt' but still refused insanity verdict, foreperson says
summary: Three Lindsay Clancy jurors say a lone holdout admitted having reasonable doubt but still refused to deliver a not guilty by insanity verdict.
story: Fox News national correspondent Bryan Llenas reports on the mistrial declared in the Lindsay Clancy murder case after a Plymouth, Mass., jury deadlocked following about 40 hours of deliberation over six and a half days.

Three people who served on the jury in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial are speaking publicly for the first time after last week's mistrial, saying a lone holdout prevented the panel from reaching a unanimous verdict.

The jurors, including the foreperson, said one juror acknowledged having reasonable doubt but still refused to find Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity, according to interviews with NBC10 Boston. The jurors' accounts offer the first public glimpse inside the deliberations that ended in a deadlocked jury.
The mistrial came after days of deliberations in the closely watched case against Clancy, the Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three young children in January 2023.
"He admitted he had reasonable doubt and I started filling out the forms, I was so excited," the foreperson told NBC10 Boston.
LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE CALLS MISTRIAL, THEN GRANTS DEFENSE ONE HOUR STAY FOR APPEAL
Lindsay Clancy looks at jurors as Judge Sullivan asks them to start deliberations for a sixth day during her murder trial on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger)
But the foreperson said the juror then added, "But I'm still not going to say that she's not guilty by reason of insanity."
The foreperson said she had already begun completing the verdict paperwork after believing the jury had reached an agreement.

"There were three forms I had to fill out, and I started filling them out. I wrote my signature on each one," she told the station. "But then he said, 'But I'm still not going to say she's not guilty by reason of insanity.'"
LINDSAY CLANCY ATTORNEY KEVIN REDDINGTON SIGNALS HE'S OPEN TO A DEAL, HOPES DA WILL 'REVISIT' CASE
Lindsay Clancy sits at the defense table during her murder trial at Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass., Wednesday, August 5, 2026. (David L. Ryan/Pool)

Clancy admitted to the killings but pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity, arguing she was suffering from severe mental illness at the time. Prosecutors maintained she was criminally responsible for the deaths.

The foreperson also told the station she wrote the note to the judge raising concerns that one juror had expressed reasonable doubt but would not agree to a verdict. The three jurors said they became frustrated with the holdout during deliberations, claiming he refused to consider the views of the rest of the panel.
"He was very arrogant. He really did not take anything that anybody said," one juror told NBC10 Boston.
The juror said the holdout questioned evidence about Clancy's medications even after the panel reviewed toxicology reports from South Shore Hospital that had been admitted into evidence.
MOM ‘VERY INVESTED’ IN LINDSAY CLANCY CASE HIRES CASEY ANTHONY ATTORNEY AFTER ALLEGEDLY KILLING SON: DOCS
Lindsay Clancy's attorney, Kevin Reddington, speaks outside the courthouse after the third day of deliberations in her murder trial on Aug. 31, 2026. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
"There were nurses on the jury. Yes, they spoke to that specific thing," the juror said. "That was a question that he had, and he just completely disregarded the information that they gave him."

"Every one of us in the hours of our frustration would get up and walk the room because you just couldn't sit anymore," another juror told the station. "He would not interact with us and try to understand."

The juror said the panel repeatedly read the judge's instructions on reasonable doubt to the holdout. "We read to him, on numerous occasions, the definition of reasonable doubt from Judge Sullivan's instruction," she said.

The same juror said the holdout "had the hardest time getting over the fact that Lindsay viciously killed her children," despite the panel's discussions about whether Clancy met the legal standard for insanity.
NBC10 Boston reported it attempted to contact the juror identified by the others as the holdout but had not received a response.
Lindsay Clancy attends her murder trial at Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth on July 29, 2026.  (David L. Ryan/Pool)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
A judge declared a mistrial last week after jurors informed the court they were hopelessly deadlocked following several days of deliberations.
It remains unclear whether prosecutors will seek to retry the case.

title: Virginia county to pay up to $2K to families with primary wage earner detained by ICE
summary: Arlington County approved $50,000 to support immigrant families whose primary wage earner has been detained amid Trump administration enforcement efforts.
story: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents arrest more than 1,300 illegal immigrants in a massive Washington, D.C. area sweep known as Operation Safe Community. 'Fox & Friends' co-hosts break down the arrests of MS-13 gang members and a suspect tied to student fentanyl overdoses. The operation highlights growing concerns over border security and local community safety.
Leaders in one Virginia county approved a program last week to set aside $50,000 to support families in which the primary wage earner has been detained by federal immigration authorities.

In a special Sept. 2 meeting, the Arlington County Board voted 4-0 to appropriate the funds, which will be distributed by Arlington Thrive, which describes itself as a "key component of the social safety net" in partnership with the county government.

Under the program, eligible families will receive up to $2,000 for those who have lost the primary wage earner. Arlington Thrive aims to assist between 25 to 30 families, according to the board's agenda.

The move was in response to the Trump administration's illegal immigration enforcement efforts in the Washington, D.C., area in recent months.

"Ensuring that we take care of our community and our residents and our people does mean making sure that we have emergency assistance available for what is probably one of the most challenging situations that you could possibly face," Board Vice Chair Maureen Coffey said. "I'm very proud of us for doing this."

ILLINOIS MOTHER CHARGED WITH MURDER IN DEATH OF 2-YEAR-OLD SON IN CASE DRAWING COMPARISONS TO LINDSAY CLANCY

title: United flight attendant makes quick save, catching baby that was about to fall from 'exhausted' mom's lap

story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A flight attendant aboard a United Airlines flight sprang into action when an exhausted mother dozed off and her baby began slipping from her lap — catching the child before offering to hold the baby so the weary mom could get some much-needed rest.

Passenger John Frehse shared the touching encounter on Instagram, praising flight attendant Monique Harris for her quick response aboard United flight 3486 from Newark, New Jersey, to Grand Rapids, Michigan.
"United should be very proud," Frehse wrote, adding that the new mother had fallen asleep when her baby was "about to fall out of her lap."
PILOT MARRIES VEGAS-BOUND COUPLE MID-FLIGHT AS 178 PASSENGERS BECOME WEDDING GUESTS
Passenger John Frehse shared the touching encounter between flight attendant Monique Harris and family on Instagram. (Instagram/ woodylovestravel)

Frehse tagged United CEO Scott Kirby in the post and said he has flown more than 2 million miles with the airline.
"She is an A+ employee," he wrote. "Take note!!!"

Flight attendant Monique Harris was praised for her quick response aboard United flight 3486 from Newark, New Jersey, to Grand Rapids, Michigan. (Facebook/Monique Unique Harris)

story: Former NTSB investigator Dr. Alan Diehl joins ‘Fox News Live’ to analyze possible factors behind an Amazon cargo plane’s deadly runway overrun at Miami International Airport.
Authorities in Miami identified the five people killed when an Amazon cargo plane overran a runway while landing at Miami International Airport on Sunday, crashing into vehicles and catching on fire.

The plane then "continued into the grass and impacted another fence line, which separated an area where Tesla robotaxis were stationed," Homendy said.

title: Smithsonian head Lonnie Bunch to retire amid allegations of far-left woke messaging at museums
summary: Lonnie Bunch III announced his retirement from the Smithsonian Institution amid an escalating clash with the Trump administration over museum leadership.
story: Laura Ingraham exposes the left-wing curators behind radical exhibits at the Smithsonian. Historian Dr. Jody Edward Ginn joins 'The Ingraham Angle' to discuss the bias and exclusion of conservative perspectives in national museums.

The head of the Smithsonian Institution announced his retirement Tuesday, stepping down amid an escalating clash with the Trump administration over the leadership and direction of the nation’s museums.

Lonnie Bunch III, who has led the Smithsonian since 2019 and was the founding director of the National Museum of African American History and Culture, said he will leave the post by the end of the year.

"It is with very mixed emotions and heartfelt gratitude that I announce my retirement from the Smithsonian," Bunch said in a press release. "I have spent nearly half of my life working at and being part of the Smithsonian family, and what a privilege it has been. There is no place like the Smithsonian — it has been one of the great loves of my life, and I am extraordinarily proud of what we have accomplished together."
SMITHSONIAN SHOWDOWN INTENSIFIES AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION ISSUES A STARK NEW WARNING
Lonnie Bunch III speaks during the Smithsonian Latino Museum Reception on June 16, 2022, in Washington, D.C. (Photo by Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images for Smithsonian Latino Museum)
"I leave with pride and sadness, gratitude and joy, and with enormous confidence in the people who will carry this remarkable institution forward," he added.

Bunch’s departure comes as the Trump administration has intensified scrutiny of the Smithsonian, accusing its leadership of allowing progressive ideology to shape its presentation of American history and raising concerns about potential violations of federal nondiscrimination law.

In a letter recently made public by the Department of the Interior, the administration said the Smithsonian leadership’s "institutional culture may have resulted in significant violations of Federal antidiscrimination law," including allegedly creating a hostile work environment and allocating opportunities, funding and other benefits based on race, ethnicity and other protected characteristics.
The Smithsonian, the nation's largest museum and research complex, is at the center of a White House campaign to overhaul its presentation of American history. (J. David Ake/Getty Images)
The letter did not include specific evidence of illegal activity, and the Department of the Interior did not provide further information when previously reached for comment by Fox News Digital.

The administration warned that federal agencies could withdraw certain forms of support if its concerns are not addressed, saying an "appropriate response" from the Smithsonian "must likewise address executive leadership and institutional ideology."

The Smithsonian's National Museum of American History is being called out for being 'ideologically captured' and presenting woke revisionist history on the weekend of America's 250th birthday. (Kevin Carter/Getty)
The pressure follows a 2025 executive order directing officials to seek the removal of what the administration called "improper ideology" from the Smithsonian.
SMITHSONIAN'S TAXPAYER FUNDS FACE CHOPPING BLOCK AS GOP DEMANDS ACCOUNTABILITY FOR 'WOKE' HISTORY

Bunch became the Smithsonian’s 14th secretary in June 2019, making him the first African American and first historian to hold the position. He previously led the creation of the National Museum of African American History and Culture, serving as its founding director from 2005 through its opening in 2016.
Bunch first joined the Smithsonian in 1978 and has spent nearly four decades at the institution, apart from a period when he served as president of the Chicago Historical Society.
The Smithsonian National Museum of American History in Washington, D.C., on Sunday, Oct. 12, 2025. (Stefani Reynolds/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Chief Justice John Roberts, who serves as chancellor of the Smithsonian, praised Bunch’s tenure and said the institution would work with him to ensure a smooth transition.

"From his days as a young curator at the National Air and Space and American History Museums through his tenure as the founding director of the African American History and Culture Museum and culminating in his distinguished service for the past seven years in the Smithsonian’s top job, Secretary Bunch has pursued excellence in the telling of our nation’s story," Roberts said.

Smithsonian Board of Regents Chair Franklin D. Raines said the board will announce an acting secretary and begin a national search for Bunch’s successor.
Fox News Digital’s Robert Schmad contributed to this report.
