Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: From cockroach milk to stepping on snakes, Ig Nobel awards celebrates science at its oddest
summary: Cockroach milk, kissing evolution and the underwear soil test were among the unusual real studies honored at the Ig Nobel ceremony in Zurich.
story: An Arkansas high school football player discovered a cottonmouth snake inside his helmet after completing a practice. Animal control was able to remove the two-foot reptile from the padding after he wore the equipment during practice.

A motley crew of scientists was honored this week for its unusual contributions, which included studying cockroach milk, the evolutionary history of kissing and testing soil health by using underwear.
The satirical Ig Nobel ceremony, which honors unusual but real studies, took place in Zurich Thursday and was presented by the digital magazine, the Annals of Improbable Research.
The awards, which were founded in 1991, took place outside the U.S. for the first time this year over the concern that the honorees wouldn’t be able to get a visa.

Other winners included researchers who found upper-class people were more likely to engage in unethical behavior, such as stealing candy from a baby, a study on proper nose blowing and gently stepping on snakes to see what provokes them into biting people.
WASHINGTON HOMEOWNER HEARS MYSTERIOUS BANGING CALLS 911 BEFORE POLICE FIND GROWLING BOBCAT AT TOP OF STAIRS

Soil Science Prize winners Pia Viviani, right, and Atlant Bieri, left, stand on stage during the Ig Nobel Prize ceremony at the Zurich Convention Center in Zurich, Switzerland, Thursday. (Claudio Thoma/Keystone via AP)

"The general pattern seems to be that, with wealth and rising power, you become less engaged with the needs of others and less burdened by the needs of social relationships," Dr. Paul Piff, a social psychologist at the University of California, Irvine said, according to the Guardian.
"Taking candy from children might be the least of our worries, but it’s emblematic of the tendency to prioritize one’s own needs over those of others."

The final four honorees included those studying the power of having mutual enemies, attempts at a splash-free urinal, using dead mosquitos for 3D printing and research that found parents love the smell of their newborn babies but not teenage children.

In case you’re wondering, the team studying the history of kissing has defined it as "a non-agonistic interaction involving directed, intraspecific, oral-oral contact with some movement of the lips/mouthparts and no food transfer." Romantic.

From left, Nobel Prize winners Esther Duflo, Abhijit Banerjee, Michel Mayor and Tim Hunt look at underwear handed over by the Soil Science Award winners during the Ig Nobel Prize ceremony at the Zurich Convention Center in Zurich, Switzerland, Thursday. (Claudio Thoma/Keystone via AP)
COUPLE PUBLICLY CANED AFTER ALLEGED TIKTOK KISS SPARKS OUTRAGE IN INDONESIA

"Next time you kiss someone, you can think, 'This is a 21.5 million-year-old tradition that I'm honoring here," evolutionary biologist Matilda Brindle of the University of Oxford said, according to NPR. "It's not just a modern human behavior. It's really ancestral.' And to us, that suggests that it probably has quite a useful evolutionary function."
Brindle said her team believes that Neanderthals not only kissed each other. They may have also kissed early humans.
CAVE DISCOVERY PUSHES BACK EVIDENCE OF HUMAN ANCESTORS USING FIRE TO 1.79M YEARS AGO
The winners of the Ig Nobel Prize pose for a group picture during the ceremony at the Zurich Convention Center in Zurich, Switzerland, Thursday. (Claudio Thoma/Keystone via AP)
All the honorees receive a trophy that looks like a cross between a mushroom and a human foot while the audience throws paper airplanes at them.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The Ig Nobel has no relation to the actual Nobel Prize, which will announce its honorees in October.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Apple announces long-awaited foldable phone, iPhone Duo
summary: Apple’s first foldable phone capped a day of product announcements that also included the new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.
story: Apple on Wednesday unveiled its first foldable phone, called the iPhone Duo, a device that opens like a book into a wide screen. The announcement marks the biggest change to the iPhone since it was introduced in 2007, and an entry into a category that Samsung has dominated for years.

In its announcement, made by Apple’s new CEO John Ternus at the company’s Cupertino, California, headquarters, Apple emphasized that it took time to develop the idea after rivals embraced it years ago.

“Others have created foldables that just feel like two phones awkwardly stuck together,” Ternus said in the livestreamed event. He described the Duo as having “a larger display that feels as natural and intuitive as iPad.”
Ternus said it was the “largest display ever on an iPhone, while still fitting easily in your pocket.”
Apple said the device would sell for a base price of $1,999. Preorders would start Oct. 16, and the device will be available at stores on Oct. 23, the company said.

Once opened, the double-wide screen is 50% larger than the size of the iPhone Pro Max and measures 7.6 inches on the diagonal, said Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president for worldwide marketing. He said the device is made of titanium, has speakers on the top and the bottom, and initially will come in two colors: “star white” and “night sky.”

title: Missouri redistricting fight heads back to Supreme Court
summary: WASHINGTON — The no-holds-barred redistricting fight in Missouri has returned to the U.S.
story: WASHINGTON — The no-holds-barred redistricting fight in Missouri has returned to the U.S. Supreme Court for the second time, with opponents of a new GOP-drawn congressional map urgently asking the justices to prevent it from being used in the midterm elections.

At issue is how to resolve two competing rulings, with the Missouri Supreme Court finding last week that the new map could not be used based on state law while a voter referendum that could veto it moves forward. The U.S. Supreme Court on Tuesday declined to block the state court ruling.

But in a separate case, a federal court on Tuesday ruled that the new map must be used in order to prevent violations of the U.S. Constitution, raising questions that were not put to the U.S. Supreme Court in the state case.
The Missouri Supreme Court has also opened a contempt probe into Secretary of State Denny Hoskins. A hearing is set for Thursday morning.
All of this is playing out after Tuesday’s deadline to finalize Missouri ballots ahead of this fall’s elections. First ballots are set to go out in the state on Sept. 19.

In the new U.S. Supreme Court filing, brought by a group called People Not Politicians, led by activist Richard von Glahn, lawyers said the federal judge’s ruling is in “direct conflict” with the state Supreme Court.
Hoskins has made it clear that “election officials will continue to implement a congressional map that Missouri’s highest court has held is not and never has been law,” they wrote.
Missouri-based U.S. District Judge Stephen Clark ruled on Tuesday that the state must use the map that people voted in during the primary.
The St. Louis-based 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals declined to put that ruling on hold.

Separately, the Missouri Supreme Court issued an order asking Hoskins, a Republican, to explain “why he should not be held in contempt” for violating the ruling last week that said the state cannot use the new map. Despite the ruling, Hoskins has continued to push to use the new map.
The court also ordered Hoskins to appear in person at Thursday’s hearing.
Hoskins indicated in a post on X that he would not back down.
“I look forward to my day in court,” he said.
Add to Google
Add to Google

A congressional map Missouri Republicans enacted in 2025, part of a nationwide redistricting push led by President Donald Trump, sought to eliminate one of the state’s two Democratic-held seats, currently held by Rep. Emanuel Cleaver.
Should the Missouri Supreme Court’s ruling remain in effect, a map drawn in 2022, with six Republican-held seats and two Democratic-held seats, would be in place for the general election.
The legal fight was kick-started when von Glahn’s group gathered signatures in support of a state referendum that would undo the GOP-drawn map and put it on hold for the 2026 election.

But Hoskins refused to put the measure on the ballot, arguing that redistricting plans are not subject to voters’ approval. The Missouri Supreme Court, which has a majority of Republican appointees, disagreed, saying there was nothing in state law that exempted congressional maps passed by the Legislature from being vetoed by voters via the referendum process.

title: Bessent’s move to tamp down rising rates backfires, as bond yields jump and stocks tumble
summary: Bonds sharply sold off and stocks after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s latest effort to tamp down what he called market “fever” backfired.
story: Bonds sharply sold off and stocks tumbled Wednesday after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s latest effort to tamp down what he called market “fever” backfired.

At 11 a.m. ET, the Treasury Department announced that it would repurchase $6 billion worth of 10- to 20-year government bonds, in the hopes that fewer bonds on the market would drive up demand, pushing down rates, or yields, that have soared to levels not seen in decades.

But that’s not what happened. Instead, most Treasury yields sharply jumped on the announcement. The 10-year bond yield surged to as high as 4.85%, its highest level since November 2023. The 20- and 30-year bond yields surged to as high as 5.3%. When Treasuries fall, their yields rise.
By 4p.m. ET, bond yields had pulled back slightly from the highest levels of the day but remained sharply elevated.
The Nasdaq Composite, which is sensitive to interest rates given the high number of major tech companies it tracks, ended the day down 0.6%. The S&P 500 tumbled 0.5%.

The reaction from Wall Street underscores the limits of the power Bessent claims to exert over markets. It also comes as the Trump administration is running out of tools to gain leverage over major parts of the U.S. economy, from gas prices and bond yields to retaliatory tariffs.

Yields have been rising steadily since the start of the year. But they began to surge in late July, when President Donald Trump’s newly-installed Federal Reserve chairman, Kevin Warsh, held a press conference at which he didn’t sound fully committed to using the Fed’s tools to help curb inflation.
That spooked bond markets, which saw inflation climbing as the Iran war dragged on and Trump’s trade policies raised the prices of many imported goods.

title: ‘Trumpapalooza’ and another primary night: From the Politics Desk
summary: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.
story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.

In today’s edition, we dig into the GOP’s midterm convention and the next round of primaries in Rhode Island. Plus, Andrea Mitchell writes that the aftermath of 9/11 is still being felt 25 years later.
— Adam Wollner
Sign up to receive this newsletter in your inbox every weekday here.
‘Trumpapalooza’ and another primary night
It’s a big night on the sports calendar, with the NFL season kicking off and more action at the U.S. Open.

But it’s also a big night on the political calendar, with Republicans meeting for a midterm convention in Dallas, and Rhode Island holding its primary (yes, on a Wednesday, to accommodate the late Labor Day holiday this year).

🎉 ‘Trumpapalooza’: Republicans are kicking off a two-day gathering today designed to boost enthusiasm for the party in the final stretch of the midterm campaign. In addition to hearing from the party’s candidates on the ballot across the country this fall, President Donald Trump is set to speak at 9 p.m. ET tonight, while Vice President JD Vance will address convention-goers tomorrow.

As Sahil Kapur reported, congressional Republicans have been split on whether to attend. On the one hand, speaking at a gathering headlined by Trump could help them turn out his MAGA base in key races. On the other, being tied to an unpopular president amid widespread discontent over the state of the economy and the Iran war could repel swing voters.
The latest NBC News Decision Desk poll found that Trump’s job approval rating sits at 80% among Republicans, but 24% among independents.
According to an NBC News tally, 32 House Republicans have said they will be at the convention, while 35 said they will not.

“We’ve been working really, really hard here, and it just doesn’t get out. So I’m going down there because this is a fantastic platform to tell people what we’ve been doing,” GOP Rep. Derrick Van Orden, who represents a battleground district in Wisconsin, said in an interview. “We have been accomplishing things, and it’s just so under the radar, unfortunately.”
🦀 Rhode Island primary: On the Democratic side, Gov. Dan McKee is at risk of becoming the first sitting governor to lose a primary in eight years, Adam Edelman notes.

McKee is facing a challenge from former CVS executive Helena Foulkes, who has outspent him on the airwaves 3-to-1, according to AdImpact. Foulkes also narrowly lost the 2022 primary to McKee, who replaced Gina Raimondo in 2021 when she was selected by President Joe Biden to be commerce secretary.

While there has been a wave of anti-incumbent energy in Democratic primaries throughout the year, Rhode Island’s contest hasn’t broken along generational or ideological lines. Rather, the race between Foulkes, 62, and McKee, 75, has been defined by hyperlocal issues — most notably the closure of a major bridge in Providence in 2023.
The last sitting governor to lose a primary was Republican Jeff Colyer in Kansas in 2018. He was defeated by then-Secretary of State Kris Kobach, who was backed by Trump.
🎥 Tune in to the Kornacki Cam at 7:45 p.m. ET to watch Steve break down tonight’s results.
🗳️ New Hampshire recap: As for last night, Republican former Sen. John Sununu and Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas won their Senate primaries, setting up a battleground state race, Bridget Bowman writes.
A lingering lesson, 25 years after 9/11
Those of us who covered the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks 25 years ago had reported early warnings, although there was no immediate proof.

The Environmental Protection Agency, then led by former New Jersey Gov. Christine Todd Whitman, issued the first official “all clear” about the air quality and safety of drinking water a week later, on Sept. 18. The air from the collapse of the twin towers for the first responders working in the still smoldering pit was safe, tests showed. There were reassuring pronouncements from the city’s mayor, Rudy Giuliani, and his immediate successor, Michael Bloomberg.

On Sept. 21, Whitman said that the “EPA has been very aggressive in monitoring for potential environmental problems in the aftermath of the World Trade Center attack. … New Yorkers and New Jerseyans need not be concerned about environmental issues as they return to their homes and workplaces.” She continued: “More recently, we’ve also tested drinking water supplies and found no sign of asbestos bacterial contamination, PCBs or pesticides.”

Were government officials at the local and federal level — from both political parties — misled by the experts? Or, perhaps, overly eager to reassure the public and Wall Street? Partisans on all sides still disagree. Anecdotally, residents, health officials and first responders were reporting discomfort and more serious respiratory concerns from visible dust and larger debris during the aftermath.

More definitively, the 9/11 Commission reported in 2004 that the EPA “did not have sufficient data and analysis to make such a blanket statement” one week after 9/11. Congress still resisted appeals for survivors’ benefits, even as firefighters and other first responders began succumbing to lung ailments.

On NBC News on Feb. 25, 2019, former first responder and advocate John Feal, a demolition supervisor at ground zero, told me: “Everybody knows these cancers and these respiratory illnesses have different latency periods. I mean, come on, I mean, it’s just insulting. We’re sick and dying, but we’re not stupid.” By then, he had already attended 181 funerals of fellow responders.

It took years after the attacks for Feal and his high-profile fellow advocate, Jon Stewart, to persuade Congress to approve health benefits for surviving first responders and their families, and years more to extend those family benefits until 2090.

“As I sit here today, I can’t help but think what an incredible metaphor this room is for the entire process that getting healthcare and benefits for 9/11 first responders has come to,” Stewart said in June 2019 during congressional testimony. “Behind me a filled room of 9/11 first responders and in front of me a nearly empty Congress.”

“Sick and dying, they brought themselves down here to speak to no one,” he continued. “Shameful. It’s an embarrassment to the country and a stain on this institution and you should be ashamed of yourselves, for those who aren’t here, but you won’t be because accountability doesn’t appear to be something that occurs in this chamber.”

And now, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has released 170,000 pages of documents providing substantial evidence of the environmental fallout from ground zero, including asbestos found in air samples half a mile from the twin towers 10 months after the buildings collapsed.

It perhaps serves as a cautionary tale for public policymakers who have long focused on the counterterrorism lessons of 9/11, but not the impact on first responders and others living in the shadow of the twin towers.
Owen Hayes contributed.

title: Trump admin fires prosecutor in dropped case against politically linked billionaire
summary: A federal prosecutor who had been assigned to the now-defunct case against a politically-linked Indian billionaire has been fired by the Trump administration, two people familiar with the firing tell NBC News.
story: WASHINGTON — A federal prosecutor who had been assigned to the now-defunct case against a politically linked Indian billionaire has been fired by the Trump administration, two people familiar with the firing tell NBC News.

The prosecutor, who had been with the Justice Department’s Fraud Section in Washington, was one of two who previously asked to withdraw from the Gautam Adani case two days after Principal Associate Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter moved in May to dismiss the case against Adani.

Adani was charged in November 2024 in connection with an alleged scheme to defraud U.S. investors and pay off Indian government officials to win a bid to develop the country’s largest solar power plant. He called the accusations baseless.

Adani pledged to invest billions of dollars in the U.S., and Democratic lawmakers raised questions of a quid pro quo with the Trump administration to avoid prosecution. The federal judge hearing the case ordered Adani to explain whether any deal was made in connection with the government’s significant reversal. He denied it, and so did the Justice Department.
U.S. District Judge Nicholas Garaufis of the Eastern District of New York eventually agreed to toss the case against Adani, though he blasted the Trump administration’s “highly unusual” conduct.

The prosecutor’s firing came a month later, the people said. The Trump administration has fired numerous federal employees without explanation, beyond citing Trump’s executive powers in letters, which Justice Department alumni have come to refer to as “Article II letters,” referring to a clause of the U.S. Constitution.
A spokesperson for the Eastern District of New York declined to comment. The prosecutor did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Last week, Garaufis let stand some counts against some of Adani’s co-defendants, saying the Trump administration had “not provided sufficient factual information to support the stated reasons” for dismissing the charges.

Adani had pledged to invest billions of dollars in the United States but said in a sworn statement filed in July that he was “not aware of any agreement involving any person or entity exchanging anything for the dismissal of the indictment.”

An email from May from U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella referenced a slide deck presentation from Adani’s defense team that included a proposal to invest $10 billion in the United States, and Nocella wrote that the proposal was “categorically rejected” by the office.

The Justice Department has defended the decision to forgo its case against Adani, with McCotter saying the case was “indefensible” and that he “would have sought dismissal of the securities charges regardless of any mentions of investments, regardless of whether the civil case (or any other matter) was settled or otherwise resolved.”
An attorney for Adani couldn’t be reached for comment about the prosecutor’s firing.

title: Lindsay Clancy rejects conspiracy theories accusing her ex of their children’s deaths, lawyer says
summary: In a wide-ranging interview, Kevin Reddington talked with NBC News about Clancy’s high-profile murder case in the deaths of her three children, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months old.
story: Lindsay Clancy rejects the internet conspiracy theories accusing her ex-husband of killing their three children in 2023 and believes he has been unfairly targeted by online sleuths since her murder trial, her defense attorney Kevin Reddington told NBC News on Wednesday in a wide-ranging interview.

“She knows, and it’s readily apparent that Patrick has been set upon and his life has been turned upside down into a nightmare that he doesn’t deserve. Period. Full stop,” attorney Kevin Reddington said Wednesday.

Patrick Clancy’s lawyers released a statement Tuesday responding to the online allegations and slamming the true-crime creators behind the theories. The statement called the theories and online storylines a “campaign of misinformation” that was “publishing what they know to be outright falsehoods that Patrick was somehow involved in the death of his young children and other vile claims.”
His lawyer added that “every appropriate measure will be pursued to hold them accountable, including legally,” and that “law enforcement has been notified.”

Reddington told NBC News that Clancy is aware of how the case has taken off on social media as online sleuths pushed conspiracy theories and broke down testimony about the broadcast trial and as conversation around postpartum psychosis captured the nation. She also disagrees with the theories.

On Friday, Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial at Plymouth Superior Court after the jury deliberating whether Clancy was criminally responsible for the strangulation deaths of her three children said it was deadlocked three times. Reddington sought a last-minute emergency stay to send the jurors back to deliberations, but a justice at Massachusetts’ Supreme Judicial Court swiftly denied it.
Since then, Clancy is “not very good” and remains “suicidal” after her high-profile murder trial, Reddington said.
“She’s strong. She has incredible family support,” he added of his client. “But she is suicidal. I mean, she’s on 24/7, one-on-one suicide watch. I worry about her every day.”
Add to Google
Add to Google

Despite the dramatic end to the trial that leaves Clancy’s legal case in limbo, Reddington says his client does not hold any anger toward prosecutors, jurors or even witnesses who testified against her.

“She was hurt by the way they would talk about her and the way they would attack her. She was hurt, but she never once expressed anger towards anybody in the system,” he said. “She doesn’t have it in her DNA to be angry with anyone.”
Instead, he added, she talks about her children and often repeats one phrase constantly: “I want my babies.”

The sentiment is a stark contrast to the prosecution’s case throughout the trial, which argued Clancy was aware of her actions and planned the killings ahead of time. Reddington argued that she was compelled to act on auditory hallucinations that told her to carry out the murders, a symptom of the postpartum psychosis he said she was experiencing.
Both parties admit she killed the children: Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and Callan, 8 months old.

“That was not the Lindsay that is now living amongst us,” Reddington said Wednesday. “The person that committed this atrocious act was as a result of postpartum psychosis combined with the medications that she was provided.”
Postpartum psychosis is a rare but serious condition that can affect new mothers. More severe than postpartum depression, it can cause hallucinations and other intense psychological symptoms.

To prove their argument that Clancy was not actually experiencing psychosis at the time of the killings, prosecutors repeatedly pointed to the fact that she never told anyone she was hearing voices before that night and that she hasn’t heard any since — something said to be exceedingly rare for someone experiencing psychosis.

Reddington, however, said Wednesday that Clancy told her struggles to “anyone who would listen,” including Patrick Clancy and her mother. He conceded Wednesday, though, that “she should have” told more people about the voices.
The lawyer also challenged the notion that Clancy lied about how she was feeling and that she repeated a list of symptoms to doctors that she found online.

“If she was so smart, and Googling things like psychosis, why would she not have had exactly the symptomology that you can Google about psychosis, about postpartum psychosis, [including] the voices?” he said. “What are you supposed to say? How are you supposed to say it?”
He added: “If she was faking, she would have hit it on every single cylinder. She was telling the truth. She did the best that she could. She was failed by these doctors.”
A lone holdout

After 38 hours of deliberations, the jury on Friday said it could not reach a unanimous decision, remaining deadlocked 11-1. Jurors had the option to convict Clancy of first-degree murder, second-degree murder or manslaughter or acquit her owing to lack of criminal responsibility.
Had she been found not guilty by reason of insanity, she would have been sentenced to time in a state mental health facility.

Three jurors, including the foreperson, told NBC Boston on Tuesday that the majority favored finding Clancy not guilty by lack of criminal responsibility, while one holdout wanted to convict. But that juror expressed reasonable doubt, they said, and still wouldn’t agree with the remainder of the jury.
Reddington, however, defended the juror’s right to his opinion Wednesday, saying it “doesn’t matter” what was going through his head.
“He’s got every right to do that, and I would defend that right, but not to refuse to apply the law,” Reddington said. “This is where you draw the line.”
Now, prosecutors must decide whether to retry Clancy. The next hearing in the case is scheduled for Sept. 29.

Despite telling reporters multiple times last week that he was ready to retry Clancy’s case as soon as this week, Reddington said that is not the outcome he wants and that he will file a motion to dismiss charges. He also said he would be open to plea iscussions, but would not take a deal that landed his client in jail for even a day.
Add to Google
Add to Google
Reddington on Tuesday called on President Donald Trump to offer his client a pardon, even though Clancy was tried on state charges and the president can only pardon federal charges.

He explained Wednesday that he made the suggestion because Trump “felt compelled to comment on the case” and thought that maybe Trump could reach out to colleagues in the Justice Department to influence Plymouth County District Attorney Timothy Cruz to drop the charges. Or, he theorized, Trump might even reach out to Cruz directly on the issue.
Despite such strong attention toward the case, Reddington said, he felt that there was some fundamental misunderstanding about Clancy’s situation.

“They feel that if you determine that Lindsay was and is not guilty of this crime because of lack of criminal responsibility, that in some fashion you are ignoring the loss of these three children,” he explained. “That is as far from the truth as possible.”
Reddington added that Clancy, who is in a wheelchair and has been on suicide watch since the night of the murders, is “living in hell.”

“I look back over the years, and the people that I’ve represented — been able to help, not so much help — but yes, this is the one that really has moved me,” Reddington said, agreeing it was one of the hardest of his career.

title: John Malkovich cancels Tel Aviv show after promoter fabricates statement from him on Israel
summary: John Malkovich cancelled a show in Tel Aviv after learning The Jerusalem Post unknowingly published a made-up a quote about his “solidarity” with Israeli audiences.
story: Oscar-nominated actor John Malkovich cancelled an upcoming stage performance in Tel Aviv after learning that The Jerusalem Post unknowingly published a made-up a quote attributed to him about his “closeness and solidarity” with Israeli audiences.

Malkovich, in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter on Tuesday, said a local public relations firm “hired by the Israeli promoter drafted a quote for the article that was attributed to me, though I never made the statements that were quoted, nor was I consulted before they were printed.”
“The fact that they were printed as direct quotes from me is unacceptable and untenable,” his statement read. “For this reason, I have decided I cannot participate in the Tel Aviv performance.”
The offending quote, which NBC News obtained by using The Wayback Machine internet archive, was published by The Jerusalem Post on Saturday.

It said: “I am thrilled to return to Israel and look forward to meeting the warm Israeli audience once again, to whom I feel a strong closeness and solidarity. I hope to find you happy and optimistic! Sending you much love.”
After Malkovich complained, the newspaper updated its story to include an apology from the show’s Israeli producer, Alon Yurik.

“I would like to clarify that the original press release contained a mistake, and an incorrect quote from Malkovich was included due to a misunderstanding,” Yurik stated. “I would like to take this opportunity to apologize for that.”

It also included a slightly different version of the offending quote attributed to Malkovich: “I am excited to return to Israel and would be very happy to meet again with the warm Israeli audience, with whom I feel great closeness and identification.”
Tal Spungin, the newspaper’s managing editor, said in an email to NBC News that the “difference is due to a discrepancy in the translation of the quote.”

“It was initially provided to our Hebrew-language sister publication, Walla, in Hebrew, and was then translated into English for The Jerusalem Post,” Spungin wrote. “The quote was removed from our report after the production company confirmed to us that it was fabricated, and the wording was amended in our follow-up to better reflect the nature of the ‘quote’ as it was provided in Hebrew.”

Malkovich, 72, is the latest high-profile artist who had declined to perform in Israel amid the ongoing conflicts with Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank. But he did not directly criticize Israel.

Instead, in his statement, Malkovich said he counted himself as “lucky” to have had the opportunity to perform “in countries with governments whose values or culture I do not share” and the chance to travel to places “whose view of the world may not align with mine.”

“My appearance in any country, even my own, does not constitute approval of said country’s policies, nor actions, nor its elected or unelected leaders,” his statement said. “My appearances would also not condone nor mean that I am in supposed ‘solidarity’ with any particular political cause, nor with the killing of innocents, nor with any acts of terrorism, nor any other kind of barbarity.”
Representatives for Malkovich did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Best known for his riveting roles in movies like “Dangerous Liaisons,” “In the Line of Fire” and playing himself in the surreal meta-comedy “Being John Malkovich,” he was supposed to perform “The Music Critic,” a touring comedy featuring classical music and criticism of world-famous composers, next April in Tel Aviv.
Malkovich had previously visited Israel in July 2008 as an honorary guest of the Jerusalem Film Festival.
In April 2013, Malkovich returned to Israel with his musical theater show The Infernal Comedy: Confessions of a Serial Killer.

title: Jalen Brunson to host ‘SNL’ season 52 premiere hot off of Knicks championship
summary: It’s nothing but net for “Saturday Night Live” later this month as the show announced that New York’s own Jalen Brunson will be the first host for the show’s 52nd season.
story: It’s nothing but net for “Saturday Night Live” later this month as the show announced that New York’s own Jalen Brunson will be the first host for the show’s 52nd season.
New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson is hot off the summer of his career after leading the team to the NBA Championship in June. It’s the team’s first championship league title in more than 50 years.
The sketch comedy institution announced Brunson would host on Sept. 26 with the girl group Katseye scheduled as the musical guest.
The show announced Brunson as the first of four weeks of hosts, followed by “Fifty Shades of Grey” star Dakota Johnson, “Obsession” breakout actor Inde Navarrette and comedian Shane Gillis.
Brunson’s leadership of the Knicks skyrocketed him into the national spotlight earlier this year as the team made historic comebacks in the NBA playoffs.

The 30-year-old rallied in the fourth quarter against the Cleveland Cavaliers in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference finals to overcome a 22-point deficit. Brunson scored 38 points that game and the team eventually won in overtime against the Cavaliers, setting the Knicks up for a 4-0 sweep of the conference finals.
It was considered one of the greatest postseason recoveries in the NBA until the Knicks did it again just weeks later.

The team was trailing the San Antonio Spurs as much has 29 points during the Game 4 of the NBA Finals. But the team pushed to make up the gap in what is now regarded as the biggest championship game comeback in NBA history.

Many credit Brunson’s mentality and leadership for the Knicks’ first NBA championship since 1973. He told NBC News after the stunning Game 4 rally that the team approaches each game as if they are still at 0-0 in the series.
“Whatever’s being said, positive or negative, you can’t really think about or worry about too much,” Brunson said.
Though he’s known for his stoicism on the court, Brunson has a light-hearted side that makes him a good fit for a comedy show.

He often ribs teammate and best friend Josh Hart on the podcast they host together. Brunson can also be seen trying his best not to crack a smile in their post-game press conferences, where Hart is often seen with food he had delivered to the venue.

It’s unclear whether Hart or any of Brunson’s other teammates — or any of the famous faces who sat courtside for the Knicks championship run, including Timothee Chalamet, Mariska Hargitay or Taylor Swift — may make an appearance on the “SNL” premiere. It would be a slam dunk for a show that’s known to score celebrity cameos.

title: Tate brothers denied bail by Miami judge as they fight extradition to U.K. on sex crime charges
summary: A judge denied bail for Andrew and Tristan Tate, the “manosphere” influencers who’ll now have to remain behind bars in Florida while fighting extradition to the U.K. on dozens of sex crime charges.
story: MIAMI — A federal judge on Wednesday denied bail for Andrew and Tristan Tate, the “manosphere” influencers who’ll now have to remain behind bars in Florida while fighting extradition to the United Kingdom on dozens of sex crime charges.
The brothers failed to show they were not a flight risk, a danger to the community or deserved special consideration for bail, U.S. Magistrate Judge Lauren Louis ruled.

“Based upon the foregoing, I find that Respondents have failed to meet their burden to demonstrate that they do not present a risk of flight or danger to the community, or that special circumstances warrant their release,” Louis wrote.
“Respondents have failed to demonstrate that special circumstances here warrant relief.”
U.S. judge denies the Tate brothers' bail request
Defense lawyer Joe McBride said his clients were being unfairly pre-judged and held to standards unfamiliar to Americans.
“Detention first. Evidence later, maybe,” McBride said in statement on Wednesday.
McBride said his clients are looking forward to their day in court.
“We profoundly disagree with Judge Louis’ decision to keep Andrew and Tristan in federal custody,” the attorney added.

“They have not been convicted of a crime. They have not been ordered extradited. The Court has not heard the merits of extradition because the United Kingdom has not yet filed its formal request and supporting materials.”
Andrew and Tristan Tate have been charged with dozens of counts of rape, assault and sex trafficking in the United Kingdom.

The brothers, who are dual U.K.-U.S. nationals, were taken into custody in Miami in July after prosecutors in the United Kingdom filed new charges against them. They are fighting extradition to that county.
Prosecutors in the U.K. had argued against their release, saying in a filing earlier this month that their own statements suggest the brothers intended to evade justice.

The filing also alleged they make seek to interfere with witnesses and said the brothers repeatedly sought the names of their accusers from prosecutors in exchange for a “security” fee worth tens of thousands of pounds and a promise not to publicly identify the accusers.
The Crown Prosecution Service declined the offer in an effort to safeguard  the complainants, the filing states.
McBride said the mechanisms of extradition have been patently unfair to his clients.

“The process is the punishment. Andrew and Tristan lose their liberty first and challenge the evidence later. This is the cold machinery of extradition: rules and deadlines move forward with deliberate indifference to the human lives caught inside them,” according to McBride.
“By the time the merits are heard, more than sixty days of liberty may already be gone without a finding of guilt or a judgment of extradition. No later victory can give that time back.”

A former professional kickboxer, Andrew Tate, 39, built a vast online following espousing misogynistic and hypermasculine views. He once told an interviewer that there was “no way you can be rooted in reality and not be sexist.”

U.K. prosecutors previously charged the Tates with 21 counts of rape, assault occasioning actual bodily harm and arranging or facilitating travel for sexual exploitation. Andrew Tate was also charged with controlling prostitution.

The additional charges filed last month against Andrew Tate include seven counts of rape, 15 counts of making/distributing indecent images of children and four counts of possession of extreme pornography.
Tristan Tate, 38, was charged with six additional counts of rape, sexual assault and sexual exploitation charges.
U.K authorities said the alleged crimes took place between 2010 and 2017.

The brothers also face criminal charges in Romania, where they reportedly moved in 2016 to build an online porn business and were later indicted on allegations of forming an organized criminal group, human trafficking, trafficking of minors and money laundering. They have denied the charges.
Juliette Arcodia reported from Miami and David K. Li from New York City.

title: Apple announces long-awaited foldable phone, iPhone Duo
summary: Apple’s first foldable phone capped a day of product announcements that also included the new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.
story: Apple on Wednesday unveiled its first foldable phone, called the iPhone Duo, a device that opens like a book into a wide screen. The announcement marks the biggest change to the iPhone since it was introduced in 2007, and an entry into a category that Samsung has dominated for years.

In its announcement, made by Apple’s new CEO John Ternus at the company’s Cupertino, California, headquarters, Apple emphasized that it took time to develop the idea after rivals embraced it years ago.

“Others have created foldables that just feel like two phones awkwardly stuck together,” Ternus said in the livestreamed event. He described the Duo as having “a larger display that feels as natural and intuitive as iPad.”
Ternus said it was the “largest display ever on an iPhone, while still fitting easily in your pocket.”
Apple said the device would sell for a base price of $1,999. Preorders would start Oct. 16, and the device will be available at stores on Oct. 23, the company said.

Once opened, the double-wide screen is 50% larger than the size of the iPhone Pro Max and measures 7.6 inches on the diagonal, said Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president for worldwide marketing. He said the device is made of titanium, has speakers on the top and the bottom, and initially will come in two colors: “star white” and “night sky.”

title: Wife of man killed when Amazon-branded plane overran runway files wrongful death lawsuit
summary: The wife of one of the victims killed when an Amazon-branded plane overran a runway at a Miami airport, striking an airline cleaning service van and a passenger SUV, has filed a wrongful death lawsuit.
story: The wife of one of the victims killed when an Amazon-branded plane overran a runway at a Miami airport, striking an airline cleaning service van and a passenger SUV, has filed a wrongful death lawsuit.

Yaraisi Santiso Morejon, the wife of Yoel Rodriguez Naranjo, filed the lawsuit Wednesday, three days after the fatal incident at Miami International Airport that left four others dead and five injured.
The lawsuit, which names Amazon, Amazon Air Cargo and the cargo airline 21 Air as defendants, alleges that the crash was a “foreseeable and preventable result of multiple, concurrent failures.”

The plane’s two pilots, who survived the crash, Joseph Carroll and Jaime Felipe Silva Molina, are also listed as defendants. The suit accuses them of attempting a “high-speed, tailwind-affected landing” and cites pilot error and inadequate training.

The Boeing 767-300 aircraft was on its third trip Sunday when it landed and then overran the runway, National Transportation Safety Board Chair Jennifer Homendy said. Earlier in the day, the plane had traveled from Cincinnati to Miami, and then Miami to San Juan, Puerto Rico.
It was returning from San Juan when it crashed. An Amazon spokesperson previously said that the flight was operated by 21 Air.

Homendy said that during the aircraft’s landing, it overran the runway and struck navigational aids and equipment before hitting a Ford van on airport property that was owned by Professional Ocean Service Corp., a contract cleaning service for airline companies.

The plane careened through a perimeter fence and struck a Toyota SUV that was driving on a road nearby. The aircraft continued into the grass, where it hit a fence line that separated an area where Tesla robotaxis were stationed, Homendy said.

Morejon’s attorneys said that Rodriguez Naranjo, 53, who was driving the van, died on impact. The workers were leaving their last job and were headed home when the crash occurred, attorney Mike Morgan said at a Wednesday news conference. Four of his colleagues were also killed. They were identified Tuesday by the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office as Rolando Aleman Leon, 55; Julio C. Pineda, 75; Carlos Acosta Fajardo, 53; and Javierkys Reyes Quevedo, 47.
The cleaning company said in a statement Tuesday that it was “heartbroken” by the deaths of its workers.
One of Leon’s neighbors said he was very kind and would help take her to appointments. A family member said Leon’s son was devastated.
A neighbor of Pineda remembered him as jovial and kind, and said he was known as “El mago,” or “The Magician,” because he was always doing magic tricks.
“He was someone who was always laughing and telling stories,” Alberto Leandro said. “You’d see him and he’d crack a joke in the elevator.”
Fellow neighbor Elana Forte said Pineda was “always calm” and “always laughing.”

The Gutierrez Firm represents the families of Acosta Fajardo and Reyes Quevedo. Attorney Jorge P. Gutierrez Jr. said Acosta Fajardo was “an incredible human being, a loving husband, devoted son, cherished friend, and valued co-worker.” Reyes Quevedo’s sudden death has left his relatives and friends “heartbroken,” Gutierrez said in a statement.
Gutierrez said his office will conduct a thorough and independent investigation into what happened.

Five other people were injured and taken to the hospital. Eugenio Corredor, 79, and Ridoel Averhoff Diaz, 32, remain in critical condition, and Roosevelt Sebastian Perdomo Torres, 36, is stable, the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office said Tuesday.
Silva Molina, 37, and Carroll, 55, the two pilots, were treated and released. They could not be reached at phone numbers listed for them.
Morgan said that it appears the pilots “grossly overshot” the runway. He said that based on the information that they have and their own research, the landing spot was overshot “by over 1,000 feet.”
Morgan also accused the pilots of approaching the runway “grossly over the speed that they should have been attempting.” He said a “tailwind event” also made the landing more hazardous.
“This aircraft should have made a fly-around attempt, a go-around attempt,” he said.
The attorney also said that what they heard from the cockpit sounded “like a lot of confusion.”
“It sounds as if there is an unknowing of what to do and unknowing of the imminent danger of overshooting the runway,” he said.
21 Air did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

A spokesperson for Amazon and Amazon Air Cargo said in an updated statement Wednesday that its “deepest sympathies remain with the families, loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating tragedy.”

Amazon said it is fully cooperating with the investigation and will “continue to coordinate with 21 Air.” It also said that it has been working with officials in Miami-Dade to obtain contact information for the families affected by the crash.

Homendy said at a news conference Tuesday night that Carroll, the captain, had 7,145 hours of flight experience, according to his March 31 medical. Silva Molina, the first officer, had logged 2,655 hours as of his Aug. 13 medical, she said.

Carroll was rated to fly the type of aircraft involved in the crash in May, while Silva Molina was rated to fly it in April 2025, Homendy said. The plane was carrying more than 32,000 pounds of cargo, mostly contact lenses, when it crashed.

The cause of the crash remains under investigation. The NTSB’s investigator in charge of the probe, Chihoon Shin, said Tuesday that the aircraft’s flight data recorder showed its thrust increased during landing in a way that was consistent with a “go-around” attempt, a maneuver in which a plane aborts its landing by pulling up and circling around to try to land again.

Four seconds later, the throttles were reduced to idle power, and the landing gear brakes were reapplied, he said. Throttles were kept at idle, and the brakes remained applied until the end of the recording, Shin said, noting that “the speed brakes and the thrust reversers were not deployed.”

Speed brakes are active flaps commonly deployed to help an aircraft slow down. Thrust reversers are typically used on passenger jets upon landing, also to help it slow down. Shin said it was way too soon to know why the speed brakes and thrust reversers weren’t deployed.

title: Bessent’s move to tamp down rising rates backfires, as bond yields jump and stocks tumble
summary: Bonds sharply sold off and stocks after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s latest effort to tamp down what he called market “fever” backfired.
story: Bonds sharply sold off and stocks tumbled Wednesday after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s latest effort to tamp down what he called market “fever” backfired.

At 11 a.m. ET, the Treasury Department announced that it would repurchase $6 billion worth of 10- to 20-year government bonds, in the hopes that fewer bonds on the market would drive up demand, pushing down rates, or yields, that have soared to levels not seen in decades.

But that’s not what happened. Instead, most Treasury yields sharply jumped on the announcement. The 10-year bond yield surged to as high as 4.85%, its highest level since November 2023. The 20- and 30-year bond yields surged to as high as 5.3%. When Treasuries fall, their yields rise.
By 4p.m. ET, bond yields had pulled back slightly from the highest levels of the day but remained sharply elevated.
The Nasdaq Composite, which is sensitive to interest rates given the high number of major tech companies it tracks, ended the day down 0.6%. The S&P 500 tumbled 0.5%.

The reaction from Wall Street underscores the limits of the power Bessent claims to exert over markets. It also comes as the Trump administration is running out of tools to gain leverage over major parts of the U.S. economy, from gas prices and bond yields to retaliatory tariffs.

Yields have been rising steadily since the start of the year. But they began to surge in late July, when President Donald Trump’s newly-installed Federal Reserve chairman, Kevin Warsh, held a press conference at which he didn’t sound fully committed to using the Fed’s tools to help curb inflation.
That spooked bond markets, which saw inflation climbing as the Iran war dragged on and Trump’s trade policies raised the prices of many imported goods.

title: ‘South Park’ is now ‘South America’ in dig at Apple and Google for observing Trump’s Lake Ontario order
summary: “South Park” creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone renamed their show “South America” in a not-so-subtle dig at Trump, big tech and the pair’s own corporate bosses.
story: “South Park” creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone renamed their long-running animated TV show “South America” in a not-so-subtle dig at the White House, big tech and the pair’s own corporate bosses, the producers said Tuesday.
And by Wednesday morning, Comedy Central’s website listed the show under its new MAGA-mocking title, “South America.”

President Donald Trump has long demanded that well-known geographic locations be changed to U.S.-centric titles, with his latest call to flip Lake Ontario to “Lake America”  — name changes that Google and Apple have agreed to on their map apps.
“Inspired by the bravery and patriotism of Apple and Google, we are changing the name of South Park to SOUTH AMERICA,” producers of the six-time Emmy winning show said in statement Tuesday.
Parker and Stone didn’t spare the hand that feeds them, the Trump-approved media conglomerate Paramount Skydance.
“We especially want to thank our parent company Paramount — a Skydance Capitulation,” the pair added.
The 29th season of the show formerly known as “South Park” is set to premiere next Wednesday at 10 p.m. ET/PT on the Paramount Skydance -owned Comedy Central.
TV Guide still listed the show as “South Park” on Wednesday morning.
Google, Apple, Paramount and the White House did not immediately respond to NBC News requests for comment Wednesday.

The irreverent and Emmy-winning animated satire has been skewering American life since 1997. Its most recent seasons took a decidedly anti-Trump turn, featuring a caricature of the president impregnating Satan.

title: Apple just launched a folding iPhone — here’s what you need to know
summary: Apple just unveiled its first folding iPhone alongside five other major product launches. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new.
story: Today, Apple’s new CEO, John Ternus, announced a handful of new iPhones, Apple Watches and AirPods. It was Ternus’ first big announcement since taking over for Tim Cook earlier this month. The most newsworthy addition to the lineup? A long-rumored foldable phone (more on that below). Below is everything you need to know about these new launches — including pre-order and in-store dates.
New iPhones

Apple announced three new iPhones: the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone Pro Max and the all-new foldable iPhone Duo. Notably absent was a standard iPhone 18 — Apple may be holding that model, along with a new iPhone 18e, until spring 2027.
iPhone 18 Pro

The Pro lineup keeps a familiar look but gains Apple’s new A20 Pro chip, built on a 2-nanometer process, along with a variable-aperture 48-megapixel main camera for better low-light and depth control. This phone is $100 more expensive than last year’s model, starting at $1,199.

Apple also announced the iPhone 18 Pro Max, which starts at $1,299. The major difference between the two is screen size and battery life. The Pro has a 6.3-inch screen compared to the Max’s 6.9-inch screen. As for battery, the Pro offers up to 24 hours, while the Max offers up to 30 hours. Pre-orders for these phones open Saturday, September 12, with devices in stores September 18.
iPhone Duo

This is the big one: Apple’s first-ever foldable iPhone. It opens like a book into a roughly 7.8-inch interior display, with a smaller exterior screen for everyday use when it’s closed. Closed, it’s about the size of a passport. Apple built the Duo around its new in-house C2 modem — the company’s second-generation cellular chip, which Apple says is 50 percent faster than its predecessor while using 15 percent less power. The dual rear camera system can be used on both sides of the fold at once, so you can show someone what you’re seeing on a FaceTime call. Apple also packed in two separate battery cells, rating the Duo for up to 44 hours of use on the outer display alone, or about 24 hours using both screens.

The iPhone Duo will launch with two color options — white and dark blue. Pricing will start at $1,999 for 256GB of storage and the release is on a later schedule than the rest of the lineup: pre-orders begin October 16, with the device arriving in stores October 23.
Apple Watch

Apple also refreshed its smartwatch lineup with the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 — and, in a bit of good news, neither watch got a price increase. Both watches are available for pre-order now.
Apple Watch Series 12

The Apple Watch Series 12 centers on a redesigned Health Sensing System, paired with the new S11 chip. Its optical and electrical sensors have been rebuilt with larger, more power-efficient green LEDs, enabling far more frequent monitoring — the watch takes background heart rate readings every five seconds and measures heart rate variability as often as every five minutes, which Apple says is 60 times more frequent than on the Series 11. That data feeds a new Readiness score, calculated each morning from recent activity, vitals, and sleep, giving wearers a single number to gauge how much they can take on that day. It’s available in eight finishes, including two ceramic options in Pearl White and Night Blue, and the aluminum models now use Ceramic Shield 2, which Apple says is 60 percent tougher than the previous Ion-X glass.

Beyond health tracking, the Series 12 adds AI-driven software features tied to the new Siri, including a Live Rewind function that lets you replay the last 15 seconds of audio you just missed, and Siri Recap, which generates summaries of conversations picked up by the watch’s microphone. It retains the familiar 42mm and 46mm case sizes and standard safety features like Fall Detection and Emergency SOS, and is rated WR50 and IP6X for water and dust resistance. It starts at $399, the same price as the Series 11, and is available for pre-order now ahead of a September 18 release.
Apple Watch Ultra 4

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is built around the same S11 chip and redesigned Health Sensing System as the Series 12, but tuned for endurance athletes and outdoor use. Battery life gets a major boost too: Apple rates it for up to 50 hours of everyday use, up to 18 hours of standard workout tracking with full GPS and heart rate monitoring, and up to 45 hours in a new Max Extended Workout mode — enough to cover a 100-mile race. It’s available in two titanium finishes, natural and black, and retains the built-in satellite communications that let wearers stay connected off the grid.

Like the Series 12, the Ultra 4 also picks up Siri AI and Audio Intelligence features powered by the S11 chip, plus the ability to start a request on iPhone and pick it up seamlessly on the watch. It keeps the rugged design and precision dual-frequency GPS that have defined the Ultra line. Pricing holds steady at $799, the same as the Ultra 3, with pre-orders open now for the September 18 release.
AirPods
Apple unveiled the AirPods 5, its next mainstream earbuds, priced at $129, or $149 for the version with a wireless charging case.
AirPods 5

The AirPods 5 deliver up to 1.5x more active noise cancellation than the previous generation and are powered by a new H2 chip. They also have dynamic head tracking, adaptive audio to switch between noise cancelling and transparency mode, depending on your environment. Similar to other AirPod models, they also have IP57 rating for dust, sweat, and water resistance.

On the software side, they offer hands-free access to the new Siri AI and real-time Live Translation. Battery life is up to 4 hours with ANC on the base model, or 5 hours (22 total with the case) on the version with a USB-C Wireless Charging Case, which also supports Qi and Apple Watch charging. AirPods 5 are available for pre-order now, shipping September 18.
Are there any new Macs or iPads?

Nothing new was announced on that front today — this event was focused on iPhone, Watch and AirPods. Apple already refreshed the Mac mini and Mac Studio with M6 and M5 Ultra chips last month, and any further Mac or iPad updates will likely come at a separate event later this year or even next spring.
Why did some prices go up?

Apple didn’t detail its reasoning beyond pointing to component costs, but the iPhone 18 Pro price increase tracks with a broader trend this year: rising memory and storage prices have pushed up costs across phones, laptops and other electronics throughout 2026.

I am a commerce editor at NBC Selected and a journalist who regularly covers wellness, beauty, home and lifestyle. I have written about the “no-touch” phone law, the best screen protectors  and more. For this story, I researched all of Apple’s new offerings and watched their announcement event.

title: Does your dog really need its own bed?
summary: Experts weigh in on the best dog beds to keep your pet well rested. Shop Casper, Big Barker, L.L.Bean, Orvis and more based on comfort, size and quality.
story: No matter what kind of pet owner you are, it can be hard to resist letting your dog cuddle with you in bed. However, vets say it’s important to give your pup their own space to ensure both of you are resting well. That’s where a dog bed comes in: It also gives them a spot for naps or solitude throughout the day. And unlike other pet essentials, a dog bed can last for several years (so long as your pup doesn’t destroy it).

To help you find the right bed for your pet, I spoke to experts about the benefits of a dog bed and what to consider when shopping for one. I also pulled together some staff favorites and expert-recommended options to consider.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our weekly newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Best dog beds of 2026

Below, I compiled expert-recommended dog beds that can fit a variety of your pet’s needs and preferences. I also included beds NBC Selected editors’ own dogs use. Each of the following beds has a removable washable cover and, unless otherwise noted, comes in multiple sizes to ensure your dog is able to fit comfortably.
The Lola Pet Bed

This NBC Selected Pet Awards winner is a popular pick among our NBC Selected editors because of its spacious size and bolstered sides. Great for dogs of any age, the orthopedic bed comes with a quilted mattress that’s both removable and machine-washable, and it’s made from a breathable fabric for temperature regulation, according to the brand. NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin tried out the large/extra-large size for her dog Chance, an 11-year-old, 100-pound yellow lab. Not only did Malin find this bed to be extremely durable, but she could also easily curl up next to Chance when he gets anxious. “I’ve fallen asleep in there with him more than once,” she says.

Additionally, Malin’s 1-year-old, 8-pound dog, Mabel, was already a fan of Lola’s blankets, so it was no surprise that the brand’s dog bed quickly became one of her favorite places to lounge, too. Made from the same soft material as Lola’s blankets, the bed is plush and cushioned with tall sidewalls that help Mabel feel cozy and secure. Malin says the rectangular shape gives her plenty of room to stretch out, and Mabel often brings bones and puzzle toys into it while she relaxes. The bed arrives in a few pieces, but Malin says assembly is easy and takes about two minutes. (The brand sent Malin the bed to test).
Ruggable Washable Bolster Pet Bed

Though Ruggable is known for its washable rugs, the brand also has a washable pet bed for your four-legged companion. I received this bed from the brand to try out, and my 6-year-old, 15-pound havanese and bichon frise mix, Bella, instantly became obsessed. It comes in two pieces: a small memory foam mattress that sits at the center and a cushioned outer layer with raised edges that fits around it. Though Bella usually prefers to sleep with me in my bed, she now gravitates more toward this throughout the day— she loves resting her head on the sturdy bolsters, and she always snuggles into the warm sherpa material. The best part is that all covers are removable and machine-washable, so it’s easy to clean (and holds up to the washing machine very well, in my experience).
Casper Dog Bed

The Casper Dog Bed is a safe pick for most dogs, says Dr. Joe Wakshlag, professor of clinical nutrition and sports medicine and rehabilitation at Cornell College of Veterinary Medicine. It’s crafted with comfortable memory foam that supports your dog’s joints and hips, which is especially great for older dogs like Chance, says Malin. What’s more is that it works double time to entertain your dog: Its extra layer of washable microfiber material is designed to mimic the feel of pawing at loose earth minus the mess, according to the brand. When they’ve tuckered themselves out, the sides are lined with foam bolsters to operate as supportive pillows. The bed comes in three sizes: small for dogs up to 30 pounds, medium for dogs up to 60 pounds and large for dogs up to 90 pounds.
Best Friends by Sheri Cozy Cuddler

Smaller dogs who weigh under 30 pounds typically prefer beds that have a raised edge or even a pocket to nuzzle underneath, says Angela Logsdon-Hoover, a certified dog trainer and canine behaviorist. The Cozy Cuddler can help smaller dogs feel secure and less anxious while they relax — with its built-in blanket, flexible faux fur walls and plush interior, the bed allows your dog to either burrow or stretch out. Though the cover isn’t removable, the entire bed is machine-washable, according to the brand.
Big Barker Orthopedic Dog Bed

Big Barker makes beds for large dogs that weigh 50 to 250 pounds. It offers three rectangular bed types: Sleek, Headrest and Sofa, the latter of which includes bolsters on three of the four sides. Each bed comes with a machine-washable microsuede cover and is made from the brand’s proprietary foam, which it says is engineered to support the pressure curves of large breed dogs. (Large breed dogs are defined as weighing anywhere from 75 pounds to 100 pounds, according to Dr. Dana Varble, chief veterinary officer for nonprofit North American Veterinary Community.) The brand also offers a free replacement if the foam sinks or sags within 10 years. The bed comes in three sizes — large, XL and Giant — and in four colors.
Frisco Rectangular Bolster Dog Bed

Frisco’s dog bed is another favorite of Bella’s, who loves to rest her head on the bolstered sides or burrow her face into the bed’s cushioned crevices during a nap.The outer fabric is a plush faux suede that’s available in either a neutral khaki green or brown. The bed is available in three sizes: small (measuring 6.5 inches high), medium (9 inches high) and large (10 inches high).
Orvis Memory Foam Bolster Dog Bed

This Orvis orthopedic bed comes recommended by Dr. Kristen Nelson, a veterinarian and author of “Coated With Fur: A Vet’s Life,” because it has a polyester-filled, three-sided bolster; an open-cell, 3.5-inch-thick memory foam insert; and an open front with a low profile for older dogs to easily get on and off, according to the brand. It also has a water-resistant liner and a durable cover that unzips.
Le Dog Le Bed

This luxurious dog bed has a breathable leather outer cover that’s cooling, easy to spot clean and doesn’t retain odor, says former NBC Selected associate reporter Bianca Alvarez, who received one from Le Dog for her 7-year-old pitbull. Its dense, cooling gel memory foam interior also relieves any pressure points while providing extra comfort, according to the brand.
Furhaven Pet Bed

This L-shaped bed from Furhaven has bolsters that provide a corner sofa design for your dog, according to the brand. It’s wrapped in an easy-to-clean microsuede and includes a plush faux fur lining to help keep your canine companion snug, according to Furhaven. It has an orthopedic foam cushioning for support, which experts say can be good for older dogs. The bed’s rectangular shape makes it a comfortable option for the corner of your dog’s favorite room and its jumbo plus size is “great for big dogs like Chance — although my tiny kitten also loves stretching out on it,” says Malin.
Best Friends by Sheri The Original Calming Donut

Former NBC Selected social commerce editor Sadhana Daruvuri says her dog, Bandit, has loved this cozy circular bed since the day he came home — he likes to curl up inside when he’s napping or playing with toys. “I love how easy it is to clean; I just throw it in the wash on the gentle cycle,” says Daruvuri. It’s also another favorite of Bella’s, who loves to snuggle against the bolsters, burrow in its deep crevices and sprawl while laying on it. The bed is covered in vegan shag fur and it’s available in five sizes, with the smallest size accommodating pets weighing up to seven pounds and the largest for pets up to 150 pounds, according to the brand.
L.L.Bean Plush Cuddler Dog Bed

This L.L.Bean bed is a favorite of Nelson’s golden retriever, Sully, who likes lying in it when he’s cold. It has a warm and washable polyester fleece cover, which zips off for easy cleaning. The bed also comes with three bolstered sides that can provide a spot for dogs to rest their head. If you prefer a non-bolstered fleece option, L.L.Bean has a rectangular bed with soft polyfill cushioning.
Lesure Calming Donut Bed

This bolster dog bed comes in six stylish designs to fit your (and your pup’s) personal style, including clouds, flowers and checkerboard. Lesure sent me this bed for Bella to try out, and she loves laying on the warm, soft Sherpa material. Plus, it provides a great amount of cushion and support throughout the day. The bed is designed for dogs and cats up to 25 pounds, and it has a washable cover for easy cleaning.
Lesure Outdoor Dog Bed

Backyard activities or hiking adventures call for a bed that isn’t just waterproof but can also stand up to the elements and keep your dog safe. This washable, portable and water-resistant bed checks all those boxes. According to the brand, Lesure’s Outdoor Dog Bed features three inches of egg crate-textured foam designed to enhance airflow for cooling and conform to your pet’s body for personalized support. It includes a water-resistant, machine-washable cover equipped with a hidden zipper to deter chewing. Thanks to its lightweight design, the bed can effortlessly be moved between indoor spaces, backyards, and patios.
Kuranda Chew-Proof Elevated Dog Bed

The Kuranda Standard Dog Bed, which is one of our best overall cooling dog beds, is one of Nelson’s favorites due to its durability. “When [Sully] was a puppy, the only bed he didn’t chew up was the Kuranda platform bed,” she says. Your dog can use this bed, which is made for dogs up to 100 pounds, both indoors and outdoors. It stands on a strong, chew-proof frame that resists fading from the sun’s UV rays, according to the brand. It’s great for any type of weather, too: The air circulation underneath the bed can help keep dogs cool in summer and it’s lifted up off cold floors in the wintertime, according to Kuranda. The bed is made from smooth nylon and durable PVC, and you can choose from three large sizes and four fabric colors.
Majestic Pet Products Chevron Bolster Dog Bed

This no-frills bed is great for dogs who tend to chew or rip apart their beds. “Anyone who has a lab knows that everything becomes a chew toy — including beds — [and] Chance has yet to chew through this bed,” says Malin, adding that her dog likes to rest his head on the bolster edges. It has a washable, water-resistant cover and is available in multiple colors, including sage, burnt orange and yellow.
How I picked the best dog beds
Below are a few key factors the experts I spoke to recommend considering when shopping for a dog bed, all of which I kept in mind when curating our picks:

Size: The right sized bed means it’s large enough for your pet to sprawl out with their limbs fully extended and their entire body still on the bed, experts say. Most beds will have size recommendations based on your dog’s weight. Small dogs can generally use beds meant for bigger dogs as long as they can comfortably step in and out of it (though this is not true for medium and large sized dogs).Washability: Whether your dog tracks in dirt from the park or is prone to accidents, consider a bed that comes with a removable, machine-washable cover and, ideally, an impermeable inner cover. This will not only keep your pup’s safe space clean, but it’ll also ensure the bed lasts longer, vets say.Cushioning and support: If your dog wants or needs extra support, consider beds with thick memory or orthopedic foam, especially if you have an older dog. For older dogs who need more cushioning, consider foam that’s around 4 to 5 inches thick, says Wakshlag.Durability: How durable a bed is really comes down to your dog’s temperament. Though most dog beds are made of soft polyester designed to look good and feel comfortable, dogs more prone to chewing or pawing at their bed will likely benefit from ballistic fabrics designed to be hard-wearing. If your dog tends to destroy their toys, a soft fleece bed or one with tassels and threads should be off the table.Insulation: If you live in a colder climate, consider a bed made of fleece or other thick materials. For warmer weather, look for beds made of a cooling foam or ones that are elevated off the floor (like a cot with a mesh base) to help air circulate from the bottom.

How to shop for a dog bed

There are many types of dog beds on the market, including decorative ones that blend in with the furniture in your house, and supportive orthopedic beds that older pets find more comfortable. Consider a few different features as you shop for a dog bed, including the size of the bed, cushioning and insulation level.

The size of the bed will likely have the biggest effect on how comfortable your dog is when using it. “A bed should be large enough for your pet to lay out with their limbs fully extended with their entire body, even their toes, on the bed,” says Varble. Small dogs can usually use beds that are designed for larger breeds as long as they’re able to jump into the bed without issue, but “a tiny bed for a giant body doesn’t work very well,” says Dr. Sarah Hoggan, medical director for VCA California Veterinary Specialists — Murrieta.

If your dog tends to have accidents or likes to lie in bed after a messy trip to the park, you might want to consider a bed that has a removable outer cover and an impermeable inner cover. “Given dogs are not particularly driven by tidiness, getting a bed with a waterproof and washable cover is advised — humans prefer things in their homes not to carry the fragrance of whatever was available to roll upon outside,” says Hoggan. And with the often high price tag of some quality memory foam beds, a durable, water-resistant cover will make the bed last and ensure you’re getting your money’s worth, says Wakshlag.

In addition to an appropriate size, an adequate amount of cushioning can determine the bed’s comfort level. The amount of cushioning you need varies based on your pet’s size, level of mobility and overall health. Beds with adequate cushioning and memory foam are extremely beneficial for older dogs, especially those with arthritis, neurologic problems and orthopedic issues, says Wakshlag. “A small puppy won’t need as much cushion as a large, arthritic dog — typically, a less mobile dog will need a sturdier, thicker foam to support their body comfortably and prevent pressure sores,” says Hoggan.

Beds labeled as orthopedic dog beds, which are made with high-quality orthopedic foam to gently cushion bones and joints, are usually the best option for older dogs, says Dr. Gabrielle Fadl, director of primary care at Bond Vet.

“Unfortunately, many older large-breed dogs like to lie on the floor, which can be harder on their joints. This might be due to temperature concerns, so beds that are designed to keep a dog cool might be a good option [and] many orthopedic dog beds have this feature,” says Fadl. Orthopedic beds with a low profile on one side can allow for easier access, especially since arthritic dogs can find it hard to lift their paws high enough to get in, says Nelson.

It can also be important to look at the thickness of the foam to determine how much cushion is actually being provided to older dogs. “Anything that has 1 inch of memory foam is going to claim to be an orthopedic bed, but there’s not a lot of real evidence as to [whether it’ll actually help] — the reality is all memory foam somewhere in the 4 inches to 5 inches range is probably a good choice because that really helps with pressure distribution,” says Wakshlag.

Dog beds come in a variety of materials, ranging from soft polyester that’s designed to be attractive and comfortable to ballistic fabrics designed to be hard-wearing and durable. “If you have a dog that likes to tear apart stuffed toys, a soft fluffy fleece bed will not survive very well and your money would be better spent on something stouter,” says Hoggan.

You should also be careful with any tassels or long threads that are visible on the bed. “Dogs like to chew and a tassel or thread has the potential to become a linear foreign body trapped in their stomach and intestines,” says Hoggan.

Since beds can be a key source of comfort for your pet, consider the insulation level based on the climate you live in and the breed of your dog. Basically, the bed shouldn’t make them feel too warm or too cold.

“A thin and small breed with no undercoat, like a whippet or Italian Greyhound, will need much more warmth provided in cold northern climate, whereas an arctic breed would need a more cooling bed in a tropical region,” says Hoggan.

Beds to help warm up your dog can be made from fleece or other thicker materials, while cooling beds can either consist of a cooling type of foam or be elevated off the floor — like a cot with a mesh base — that can help air circulate from the bottom.
Frequently asked questions
Dog beds technically aren’t crucial for the health of most dogs, but they do give dogs a comfortable and safe place to rest that’s entirely their own.

“Dog beds do have the benefit of giving a dog their own personal space where they feel safe and secure. This can help with anxiety, especially if a dog needs to travel, [since] their bed can travel with them to provide comfort and familiarity,” says Fadl. Experts say a dog bed doesn’t have to be a large investment when it comes to puppies and healthy dogs — usually, any dog bed from your local store will be a good fit, says Wakshlag.

There are two main types of dog beds: basic and specialty. “The most basic beds are the kind you find in a bin at Costco — one size, one shape, soft cushion and cover,” says Hoggan, noting that these basic beds can be a great option for a young, healthy dog with no mobility issues. Specialty beds, on the other hand, are usually beneficial when there’s a medical need. This includes orthopedic and cooling features, and they’re designed to improve circulation and recovery. In essence, “the bed type depends on the dog it is meant to serve,” says Hoggan.

You can place your dog’s bed on the floor, in an open crate or in any other location where they feel sheltered and safe. “In a home, it is also a safe space, like a ‘base’ when you played tag as children — if you were on base, no one could get you,” says Hoggan. “If they’re tired and don’t want to play, they can go to bed and lie down [to tell] their family they want to rest,” she says. They’ll also go to their bed when they feel overwhelmed, especially by houseguests, children or exuberant adults.

Though many people enjoy co-sleeping with their pet, it can pose a risk for a dog if they’re small or arthritic, especially if it is a high bed. “A small dog’s legs are only about six inches to eight inches long, and the average bed height is 24 inches — premium mattresses tend to be even taller,” says Hoggan. “Jumping down from a height that is three- to four-fold the length of their legs is inviting injury.” Even if the damage isn’t immediate, that much activity can predispose them to arthritis in their back and joints at a younger age. For larger breeds, any repeated jumping can irritate arthritic conditions. “Having their own bed that is low and easy for them to enter and exit is safer and more comfortable,” says Hoggan.
