summary: The Lenovo L32p-30 31.5-inch 4K monitor is 29% off during Lenovo’s Labor Day sale. Shop the deal before the sale ends Sept. 13.
story: Upgrading to a large 4K display for your desktop can be costly, but a quality monitor significantly improves your setup if you are working remotely, studying or gaming. Lenovo is currently offering a more budget-friendly way to make that transition.

As part of Lenovo’s Labor Day promotion through Sept. 13, the 31.5-inch Lenovo 4K monitor is on sale for  29% off, lowering the cost to $329.99. title: Wife of man killed when Amazon-branded plane overran runway files wrongful death lawsuit
summary: The wife of one of the victims killed when an Amazon-branded plane overran a runway at a Miami airport, striking an airline cleaning service van and a passenger SUV, has filed a wrongful death lawsuit.
story: The wife of one of the victims killed when an Amazon-branded plane overran a runway at a Miami airport, striking an airline cleaning service van and a passenger SUV, has filed a wrongful death lawsuit.

Yaraisi Santiso Morejon, the wife of Yoel Rodriguez Naranjo, filed the lawsuit Wednesday, three days after the fatal incident at Miami International Airport that left four others dead and five injured.
The lawsuit, which names Amazon, Amazon Air Cargo and the cargo airline 21 Air as defendants, alleges that the crash was a “foreseeable and preventable result of multiple, concurrent failures.”

The plane’s two pilots, who survived the crash, Joseph Carroll and Jaime Felipe Silva Molina, are also listed as defendants. The suit accuses them of attempting a “high-speed, tailwind-affected landing” and cites pilot error and inadequate training.

The Boeing 767-300 aircraft was on its third trip Sunday when it landed and then overran the runway, National Transportation Safety Board Chair Jennifer Homendy said. Earlier in the day, the plane had traveled from Cincinnati to Miami, and then Miami to San Juan, Puerto Rico.
It was returning from San Juan when it crashed. An Amazon spokesperson previously said that the flight was operated by 21 Air.

Homendy said that during the aircraft’s landing, it overran the runway and struck navigational aids and equipment before hitting a Ford van on airport property that was owned by Professional Ocean Service Corp., a contract cleaning service for airline companies.

The plane careened through a perimeter fence and struck a Toyota SUV that was driving on a road nearby. The aircraft continued into the grass, where it hit a fence line that separated an area where Tesla robotaxis were stationed, Homendy said.

Morejon’s attorneys said that Rodriguez Naranjo, 53, who was driving the van, died on impact. The workers were leaving their last job and were headed home when the crash occurred, attorney Mike Morgan said at a Wednesday news conference. Four of his colleagues were also killed. They were identified Tuesday by the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office as Rolando Aleman Leon, 55; Julio C. Pineda, 75; Carlos Acosta Fajardo, 53; and Javierkys Reyes Quevedo, 47.
The cleaning company said in a statement Tuesday that it was “heartbroken” by the deaths of its workers.
One of Leon’s neighbors said he was very kind and would help take her to appointments. A family member said Leon’s son was devastated.
A neighbor of Pineda remembered him as jovial and kind, and said he was known as “El mago,” or “The Magician,” because he was always doing magic tricks.
“He was someone who was always laughing and telling stories,” Alberto Leandro said. “You’d see him and he’d crack a joke in the elevator.”
Fellow neighbor Elana Forte said Pineda was “always calm” and “always laughing.”

The Gutierrez Firm represents the families of Acosta Fajardo and Reyes Quevedo. Attorney Jorge P. Gutierrez Jr. said Acosta Fajardo was “an incredible human being, a loving husband, devoted son, cherished friend, and valued co-worker.” Reyes Quevedo’s sudden death has left his relatives and friends “heartbroken,” Gutierrez said in a statement.
Gutierrez said his office will conduct a thorough and independent investigation into what happened.

Five other people were injured and taken to the hospital. Eugenio Corredor, 79, and Ridoel Averhoff Diaz, 32, remain in critical condition, and Roosevelt Sebastian Perdomo Torres, 36, is stable, the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office said Tuesday.
Silva Molina, 37, and Carroll, 55, the two pilots, were treated and released. They could not be reached at phone numbers listed for them.
Morgan said that it appears the pilots “grossly overshot” the runway. He said that based on the information that they have and their own research, the landing spot was overshot “by over 1,000 feet.”
Morgan also accused the pilots of approaching the runway “grossly over the speed that they should have been attempting.” He said a “tailwind event” also made the landing more hazardous.
“This aircraft should have made a fly-around attempt, a go-around attempt,” he said.
The attorney also said that what they heard from the cockpit sounded “like a lot of confusion.”
“It sounds as if there is an unknowing of what to do and unknowing of the imminent danger of overshooting the runway,” he said.
21 Air did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

A spokesperson for Amazon and Amazon Air Cargo said in an updated statement Wednesday that its “deepest sympathies remain with the families, loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating tragedy.”

Amazon said it is fully cooperating with the investigation and will “continue to coordinate with 21 Air.” It also said that it has been working with officials in Miami-Dade to obtain contact information for the families affected by the crash.

Homendy said at a news conference Tuesday night that Carroll, the captain, had 7,145 hours of flight experience, according to his March 31 medical. Silva Molina, the first officer, had logged 2,655 hours as of his Aug. 13 medical, she said.

Carroll was rated to fly the type of aircraft involved in the crash in May, while Silva Molina was rated to fly it in April 2025, Homendy said. The plane was carrying more than 32,000 pounds of cargo, mostly contact lenses, when it crashed.

The cause of the crash remains under investigation. The NTSB’s investigator in charge of the probe, Chihoon Shin, said Tuesday that the aircraft’s flight data recorder showed its thrust increased during landing in a way that was consistent with a “go-around” attempt, a maneuver in which a plane aborts its landing by pulling up and circling around to try to land again.

Four seconds later, the throttles were reduced to idle power, and the landing gear brakes were reapplied, he said. Throttles were kept at idle, and the brakes remained applied until the end of the recording, Shin said, noting that “the speed brakes and the thrust reversers were not deployed.”

Speed brakes are active flaps commonly deployed to help an aircraft slow down. Thrust reversers are typically used on passenger jets upon landing, also to help it slow down. Shin said it was way too soon to know why the speed brakes and thrust reversers weren’t deployed.

title: Tate brothers denied bail by Miami judge as they fight extradition to U.K. on sex crime charges
summary: A judge denied bail for Andrew and Tristan Tate, the “manosphere” influencers who’ll now have to remain behind bars in Florida while fighting extradition to the U.K. on dozens of sex crime charges.
story: MIAMI — A federal judge on Wednesday denied bail for Andrew and Tristan Tate, the “manosphere” influencers who’ll now have to remain behind bars in Florida while fighting extradition to the United Kingdom on dozens of sex crime charges.
The brothers failed to show they were not a flight risk, a danger to the community or deserved special consideration for bail, U.S. Magistrate Judge Lauren Louis ruled.

“Based upon the foregoing, I find that Respondents have failed to meet their burden to demonstrate that they do not present a risk of flight or danger to the community, or that special circumstances warrant their release,” Louis wrote.
“Respondents have failed to demonstrate that special circumstances here warrant relief.”
U.S. judge denies the Tate brothers' bail request
Defense lawyer Joe McBride said his clients were being unfairly pre-judged and held to standards unfamiliar to Americans.
“Detention first. Evidence later, maybe,” McBride said in statement on Wednesday.
McBride said his clients are looking forward to their day in court.
“We profoundly disagree with Judge Louis’ decision to keep Andrew and Tristan in federal custody,” the attorney added.

“They have not been convicted of a crime. They have not been ordered extradited. The Court has not heard the merits of extradition because the United Kingdom has not yet filed its formal request and supporting materials.”
Andrew and Tristan Tate have been charged with dozens of counts of rape, assault and sex trafficking in the United Kingdom.

The brothers, who are dual U.K.-U.S. nationals, were taken into custody in Miami in July after prosecutors in the United Kingdom filed new charges against them. They are fighting extradition to that county.
Prosecutors in the U.K. had argued against their release, saying in a filing earlier this month that their own statements suggest the brothers intended to evade justice.

The filing also alleged they make seek to interfere with witnesses and said the brothers repeatedly sought the names of their accusers from prosecutors in exchange for a “security” fee worth tens of thousands of pounds and a promise not to publicly identify the accusers.
The Crown Prosecution Service declined the offer in an effort to safeguard  the complainants, the filing states.
McBride said the mechanisms of extradition have been patently unfair to his clients.

“The process is the punishment. Andrew and Tristan lose their liberty first and challenge the evidence later. This is the cold machinery of extradition: rules and deadlines move forward with deliberate indifference to the human lives caught inside them,” according to McBride.
“By the time the merits are heard, more than sixty days of liberty may already be gone without a finding of guilt or a judgment of extradition. No later victory can give that time back.”

A former professional kickboxer, Andrew Tate, 39, built a vast online following espousing misogynistic and hypermasculine views. He once told an interviewer that there was “no way you can be rooted in reality and not be sexist.”

U.K. prosecutors previously charged the Tates with 21 counts of rape, assault occasioning actual bodily harm and arranging or facilitating travel for sexual exploitation. Andrew Tate was also charged with controlling prostitution.

The additional charges filed last month against Andrew Tate include seven counts of rape, 15 counts of making/distributing indecent images of children and four counts of possession of extreme pornography.
Tristan Tate, 38, was charged with six additional counts of rape, sexual assault and sexual exploitation charges.
U.K authorities said the alleged crimes took place between 2010 and 2017.

The brothers also face criminal charges in Romania, where they reportedly moved in 2016 to build an online porn business and were later indicted on allegations of forming an organized criminal group, human trafficking, trafficking of minors and money laundering. They have denied the charges.
Juliette Arcodia reported from Miami and David K. Li from New York City.

title: Trump says firefighters near ground zero carried him to safety ‘right after’ 9/11 attacks
summary: Trump, who said that he was “down there right after this happened,” later said on Truth Social that he wasn’t at the World Trade Center “on the same day as the collapse, but shortly thereafter.”
story: WASHINGTON — At an event ahead of the 25th anniversary of 9/11, President Donald Trump told a story Tuesday in which he said two firefighters picked him up off the ground near the U.S. Steel Building close to ground zero “right after” the terrorist attacks and whisked him away because they thought the building was going to collapse on them.

“I’ll never forget two firemen, we thought it was coming down on top of us, and two firemen, big, strong guys. And I’m not the smallest guy in the world. They grabbed me under the arm, said, ‘Got to get out of here,’” Trump said, without specifying exactly when the incident occurred.

“They literally lifted me up. This is not easy to do. I’m big. They lifted me up, and they started running with me. I said, ‘Fellas, I can run myself.’ But they were amazing. But they thought it was coming down,” he added.

Trump, who said in his remarks that he was “down there right after this happened,” later said on Truth Social that he was not at the World Trade Center “on the same day as the collapse, but shortly thereafter.”
“Everything I said was exactly accurate,” he said of his remarks at the Ellipse outside the White House, sharing a TV news clip of him speaking after the attacks.

Asked for more clarity about Trump’s timeline and actions following 9/11, White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said he “was relaying his experience of a city reeling immediately after and in the days and weeks after the horrific attacks.”
Trump has told the firefighter story at least once before, during a January 2016 campaign stop in New Hampshire.
He has spoken many times about what he saw on Sept. 11, 2001, and his actions in the immediate aftermath. Here’s a look back at what he has said, much of which has not been independently verified.
August 2026: Seeing the second plane hit
In an interview with Fox News host Trey Gowdy, which aired in part Sunday, Trump said he watched as the second plane hit the South Tower of the World Trade Center.

“I’m watching, and I saw the second plane hit, and you saw that come, and you’re watching it, and it’s — because I watched the air patterns for years, and you, you know, you know where the planes are. They go up right up the Hudson River. This thing was coming right into the second building. And I said, ‘Wow!’ So I watched that happen,” Trump said in the interview, shortly after he said he watched the scene unfold from his midtown apartment.
Trump also said he went down to ground zero on Sept. 12, telling Gowdy he “worked long and hard” with a team of construction workers to help at the scene.

“I was building a building in New York, and I had a lot of construction workers. And I went down there very shortly thereafter. The following day — you couldn’t go down the same day, but, like, the following day, very, very quickly afterwards. And we worked long and hard, but it was just so terrible and so hopeless,” he said.
April 2016: Sifting through rubble
At a campaign rally in Buffalo, New York, Trump said he helped clear rubble after the attacks.
Trump was talking about “New York values,” speaking about restaurants and businesses that stayed open to help first responders and others in need.

“These people were going through terror, and you know what happened? Everyone who helped clear the rubble — and I was there, and I watched, and I helped a little bit,” Trump said, adding, “You didn’t know what was gonna come down on all of us.”
November 2015: Witnessing people jump
Trump said at a Nov. 23, 2015, campaign rally in Columbus, Ohio, that he saw people jump out of the twin towers from a window in his apartment.
Trump Tower, where Trump lived at the time, is four miles from ground zero.

“Many people jumped, and I witnessed it, I watched that. I have a view — a view in my apartment that was specifically aimed at the World Trade Center. And I watched those people jump, and I watched the second plane hit. ...  I saw the second plane hit the building, and I said, ‘Wow that’s unbelievable,’” he said.
He had told a local news station in a phone interview on Sept. 11, 2001, that he had spoken to someone that day who witnessed “at least 10 people” jumping out of the twin towers.
November 2015: Watching people cheer

Trump fed into a conspiracy theory that “thousands” of people cheered in New Jersey as the twin towers fell, telling supporters at a Nov. 21, 2015, campaign rally in Birmingham, Alabama, that he witnessed celebrations in Jersey City.
“I watched in Jersey City, New Jersey, where thousands and thousands of people were cheering as that building was coming down. Thousands of people were cheering,” Trump said.
He told George Stephanopoulos on ABC’s “This Week” in November 2015, “There were people that were cheering on the other side of New Jersey, where you have large Arab populations.”

“They were cheering as the World Trade Center came down. I know it might be not politically correct for you to talk about it, but there were people cheering as that building came down — as those buildings came down — and that tells you something. It was well covered at the time.”
There is no evidence that thousands of people celebrated in New Jersey following the attack. Local police debunked rumors at the time that people cheered.

title: Please Don’t Destroy’s Martin Herlihy Leaves ‘SNL’ After Five Years
summary: Martin Herlihy, comedy writer and of Please Don’t Destroy fame, is leaving “Saturday Night Live” after five years on the NBC sketch comedy show.
story: Martin Herlihy is leaving “Saturday Night Live” after five years on the NBC sketch comedy show.
The comedian, a writer for the program who’s also appeared in dozens of sketches, is not returning for the next season, he has confirmed.

Herlihy debuted on “SNL” in 2021 as part of comedy trio Please Don’t Destroy with fellow comedians Ben Marshall and John Higgins. The group, who produced pre-recorded digital shorts for the show, drew a significant following for their absurdist humor. Their most memorable sketches include one in which former cast member Pete Davidson features them in a music video about “Three Sad Virgins,” featuring Taylor Swift.

In another, the crew, along with actor Brendan Gleeson, play a couple of juniors who are looking forward to their final year of high school. Things go awry when Gleeson reveals that he is, in fact, a 67-year-old Irishman.

The trio’s time together on the comedy program came to an end in 2025, following Season 50. Herlihy, who has also appeared in his own solo digital shorts, remained a writer while Higgins left the show. Marshall was promoted to cast member. Please Don’t Destroy, however, has continued to perform together outside of the NBC show and is currently on tour.

Herlihy — whose father is longtime Adam Sandler collaborator Tim Herlihy, who was also once a head writer on “SNL” — joins several other recent big-name departures from the sketch comedy program. Most recently, Chloe Fineman announced in July that she would not be returning for the 52nd season.

“It’s really hard to leave ‘SNL’ but it does feel like the right time,” Fineman, who spent seven seasons on the series, wrote on Instagram. “I’m going to miss it a lot. But the people who work there are my family and that place is my home, and I know I’ll never be too far away.”

title: Kaya Scodelario Responds to Speculation That Meghan Markle Is Joining ‘The Gentlemen’
summary: Kaya Scodelario is responding to speculation about Meghan Markle will be making an appearance in the next season of “The Gentlemen.”
story: Kaya Scodelario is responding to speculation about Meghan Markle will be making an appearance in the next season of “The Gentlemen.”
“The more the merrier. Everyone, come have a go,” she said during an appearance on the 3rd Hour of TODAY on Sept. 9.
In an Aug. 21 article, Variety reported that Markle was in talks to join the third season of “The Gentlemen,” Guy Ritchie’s Netflix show.
Scodelario said she has no say in the matter, but she is following the news.
“I, unfortunately, have no decision-making abilities. I wish I did. I would love to cast the show myself. I’d put all my friends in it,” she said.
The hit Netflix series just dropped its second season and was renewed for a third.

“I think what’s wonderful about our show is that we have these characters pop up and we get these great guest actors come in, sprinkle a little bit of their magic into the characters and make really memorable scenes out of them. It’s one of the things I love most about the show,” Scodelario said.
According to IMDB, “The Gentlemen” has filmed in locations in the United Kingdom.
Markle recently moved back to the United Kingdom with her husband Prince Harry and their two children, Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, after living in the United States for several years.

Before meeting Prince Harry, Markle starred on the USA Network series “Suits” for seven seasons. After stepping back from her formal duties as a royal in 2020, Markle ventured into reality TV. She starred in two seasons of a lifestyle Netflix series titled “With Love, Meghan.”
Markle and Prince Harry also starred in a six-part Netflix docuseries “Harry & Meghan,” which featured intimate interviews and never-before-seen footage of the couple.
In 2022, Markle spoke with Variety and shared whether she’d ever return to acting.
“No. I’m done,” she said at the time. “I guess never say never, but my intention is to absolutely not.”

title: Gal Gadot Says She’s ‘Trying to Navigate’ AI and Hollywood ‘The Best Way I Can’
summary: Gal Gadot spoke about the use of AI for the movie Bitcoin and why she is defending it.
story: As conversation around artificial intelligence use in Hollywood continues to evolve, some celebrities have weighed in. Now, Gal Gadot is throwing her hat in the ring.
The actor, who stopped by Studio 1A Sept. 9 to discuss her new film “The Runner,” will soon appear in a movie called about the origins of Bitcoin.
While chatting with Gadot, TODAY’s Craig Melvin asked how the star felt about “Bitcoin” using AI for several elements of production.
“And you’re OK with this?” he asked.
Gadot acknowledged that it’s a “complex subject.”
She then shared her own take on the matter.
“AI is here and the train has left the station and it’s happening. Am I afraid of it? Am I scared of it? Yes. Am I going to look away and avoid it? No,” she said.
Rather than living in fear of AI, the actor said she’s trying to embrace it while remaining cautious.
“I’m curious to learn about AI’s benefits and hopefully without replacing humanity,” she said.
Craig then brought up the fear that AI will take human jobs, including in Hollywood, and asked what Gadot thought about the topic.
“I don’t know. I hope not. The same thing was said back in the day about moving to digital and CGI and all these things,” she said. “The truth is, I have no idea. I’m only an actress.”
“I try to navigate the best way I can,” she said.

“Bitcoin” also stars Casey Affleck, Pete Davidson and Isla Fisher. A story about the film’s production in “The Wrap” explains that it was shot on a soundstage with the set to later be filled in using AI.

Producer Ryan Kavanaugh told the publication part of the decision to use AI was because the movie is set across 200 locations. “We realized we could bring down the cost by utilizing some of the AI tools out there,” he said.

Kavanaugh also spoke about the movie’s use of AI in a LinkedIn post about the movie: “So proud of what we are doing, helping to use AI in a way that empowers creative and helps the industry move forward.”
The use of AI in Hollywood has been a hot topic. Over the summer, AI actor Tilly Norwood landed her first movie role in a film called “Misaligned,” a coming-of-age story about a girl AI bot.
Tilly’s creator, Eline Van der Velden, spoke to NBC News and denied that that AI actor’s role in the film would take work away from human actors.
“Because we would never be making a feature film, so we would never have been casting,” she said.
In July, Netflix also made headlines when the streaming service recreated the late actor Gene Wilder’s voice using AI for a reality series, with permission from his wife and estate.

Back in April, a trailer for the film “As Deep as the Grave” debuted and featured an AI-generated version of the late actor Val Kilmer. The star’s daughter gave permission for him to appear in the film.

Taylor Swift is one of several stars who have taken steps to protect her voice and likeness amid an increasing use of AI. In April, the singer filed trademark applications for two audio clips of her voice. She also filed a third trademark for an image of herself onstage.

title: Hallmark Stars and Fans Have 1 Thing in Common: They Can’t Get Enough. Here’s Why
summary: The stars and fans of the Hallmark Channel explain the network’s enduring appeal on the network’s 25th anniversary.
story: The Hallmark Channel wants to take you on a journey. Maybe it’s a dazzling getaway around the world, or back in time to another era. But the network promises its movies and TV shows will always leave you in a better place.

Whether set in idyllic small towns, merry Christmas destinations, or behind the scenes of famous places like The Plaza, Biltmore Estate, NFL stadiums, and Dollywood, the Hallmark Channel’s offerings are united in their escapism.

In these movies, old flames aren’t red flags but the right guy, finally at the right time. Family mysteries are deciphered with catharsis. Crimes are solved in cozy whodunits. Heartbreak is healed right as new love waltzes in.

That same magic was brought to The 92nd Street Y in New York on Aug. 4. for the network’s 25-year celebration, where Hallmark stars celebrated a quarter century of feel-good television with a sold-out, in-person crowd and virtual audience.
Twenty-two stars and executives gathered together for what they said felt like the ultimate family reunion, and TODAY.com was there to speak to them on the red carpet.

“You look around the room, and it’s just like all these beautiful people that you love working with,” said Marilu Henner, who has worked for the network since 2011 and starred in the “Aurora Teagarden Mysteries” series.
She was standing next to Andie MacDowell, who recently starred in “The Way Home” series, and whose first movie with the network was “Riding the Bus with My Sister” in 2005.
“Andie and I were like, “Oh, she played my daughter. Oh, he played my daughter’s boyfriend,” Henner added.
Actor Victor Webster, a member of the Hallmark family since 2012, compared the evening to “hanging out with cousins at Christmas.”
“We really look forward to spending time with each other and we value each other,” he added, standing arm-and-arm with Hallmark alum Rachel Boston.

Boston, whose first movie was, “A Ring By Spring” in 2014, said the actors have “the same desire to uplift each other and look to the positive things, and just support each other through challenging times in our lives.”
The Hallmark Channel launched on Aug. 5, 2001. Since then, the network has expanded programming and in 2024 launched their streaming service Hallmark+.

Darren Abbott, President of Hallmark Media and Hallmark Chief Brand Officer told TODAY.com, “25 years ago, someone would have said Hallmark is a greeting card company. Today, we’re so much more than the products we make or the content that we create. We’re really a caring and connecting brand. It’s all about putting goodness and love back in the world.”
What Keeps the Actors Coming Back
“When you hear Hallmark, you just think about love,” said B.J. Britt, standing with “The Groomsmen” trilogy co-stars Heather Hemmens and Tyler Hynes.
What stands out to Erin Cahill, who joined the network in 2016, is the type of love that is captured in Hallmark films — friendship, familial, romantic and self-love.

The longevity in the projects is what brings Wes Brown, whose first film was “Love Begins,” 2011 and Benjamin Ayres, who stars in “Hope Valley: 1874,” a Hallmark+ exclusive prequel series to “When Calls The Heart,” which is filming its 14th season coming back for more.
Hallmark’s actors, who often star in multiple films and series, say the casts form lasting bonds.

“I think it’s much like the heartwarming communities that we get to portray in the movies. It’s become a real-life thing,” Lacey Chabert, who has made 45 movies and two series for the network, shared.

“It’s very rare in this industry to have such supportive people with you all the time,” added Scott Michael Foster, standing next to Chabert, his co-star in the exclusive Hallmark+ limited series “Paris Is Always a Good Idea.”

The stories’ meaningful plots lead to a familial environment, sometimes literally. Hallmark veteran Alison Sweeney’s daughter Megan Sweeney made her acting debut alongside her mom in the Hallmark Channel original movie “Romance at Hope Ranch.” Ashley Williams, wrote her latest movie, “Much About Love,” with her husband Neal Dodson.
Another reason for loyalty? Hallmark Media has provided pathways for actors to not only star in movies and series, but also work behind the scenes as writers, producers and directors.

Kimberley Sustad, who recently starred in “Absolutely Devoted to You,” wrote the “Three Wise Men and a Baby” trilogy, alongside Paul Campbell. The first movie made history as cable’s most-watched movie of 2022 with 3.6 million viewers. It ranked second to Paramount network’s “Yellowstone,” per Variety.

Having three male leads wasn’t the norm for Hallmark, and Sustad told TODAY.com the project wouldn’t have come to life without the support of the network. Sustad said she feels lucky “to write things that matter to people and that make people laugh and feel love and hope.”

The impact continues behind the scenes with the “Make Her Mark” women’s directing program. Founded by actor Ashley Williams in 2023, the initiative aims to increase representation of women behind the camera through on-the-job mentorship. Crystal Lowe was the first person to go through the program and is directing her eighth movie.
“It was just time to get more women behind the camera. It’s not just about employing women, it’s about setting them up for success,” Williams said.
Add to Google
Add to Google

The collaboration that Hallmark Media encourages also frequently allows stars to incorporate important personal topics into their projects. Holly Robinson Peete, whose eldest son has autism, was able to executive produce and star in the first autism themed Christmas movie, “Our Christmas Journey” in 2021.

“For someone like me, who’s been doing television since the ‘80s, it’s very rare to find a place that you feel invests in you as a talent, and you know you’re going to work with them forever,” said Robinson Peete.

Another one of Williams’ movies, “Falling Together,” was the first to feature the Walk to End Alzheimer’s in a movie. She added a personal touch by including photos to honor her mother Linda, who had dementia, and fellow Hallmark stars, “Kentucky Roses” Andrew Walker’s mother Joyce, who had Alzheimer’s disease, and Nikki DeLoach’s father David, who had dementia.
Hallmark movies continue to feature meaningful subjects such as Parkinson’s disease, Down syndrome, IVF, foster care, adoption, divorce and cancer.

The love stories are changing, too. The first ever gay Christmas movie was Hallmark’s “The Christmas House,” in 2020, starring Jonathan Bennett. His jacket and the script are now in the Smithsonian as part of the LGBTQ+ archives.

“The biggest part about being a part of Hallmark Channel is getting to tell stories, love stories that reflect a love like mine, Bennett shared with TODAY.com. “To become so ingrained in the fabric of Hallmark Channel and LGBTQ stories has been so amazing and uplifting.”

People will come up to Bennett and tell him how meaningful his work is, “I’ll have a gay couple come up and be like, “Thank you for making that. We feel so seen. I mean, it’s just the best job in the world. I get to tell love stories on the greatest network of love.”
What Keeps the Fans Coming Back
Fans filled 92NY wearing custom T-shirts of their favorite Hallmark heartthrobs, “happy birthday” headbands, heart-shaped sunglasses, Hallmark pins, and jewelry featured in Hallmark films and more.

When superfans and sisters Anne Burger and Kathy Koabel, and their friend Cindy Francis, who saw some of the stars four times in 10 days, were asked about their custom 25th birthday T-shirts and headbands, they said in harmony, “We have to match. It’s Hallmark’s birthday. It’s like family.”

The Hallmark Channel fandom is a key part of the phenomenon. Hallmark Channel was ranked the most-watched network among women by the fourth quarter of the year for the 12th year in a row, according to Forbes.

“I can go anywhere in the world and meet someone who comes up to me with shining eyes to tell us what these movies mean in their life,” Autumn Reeser, who made her debut in “Love at the Thanksgiving Day Parade” in 2012, told TODAY.com.

Niall Matter, who starred in “Christmas at Dollywood” with Dolly Parton, said that fans often share how Hallmark films provide comfort when it comes to dealing with loss, especially at Christmas time.

When asked why she keeps watching after 25 years, fan Gwen Mordecai said, “The movies are magical, especially if you love travel, but also transports you to the kind of family and love that everybody wants to have.”
Hallmark Media creates community and connection, as Mordecai attended the 92NY event with fellow fan and friend Kim Caprio, who she met at a Hallmark store in upstate New York.
Sisters Samara and Ellie Miller were first hooked on Hallmark after watching with their mother. “It’s more than just Christmas movies. We’re all year-round watchers,” Samara Miller said.
Leaning into the fandom, Hallmark has started interactive experiences with the stars, the Christmas Experience at their headquarters in Kansas City, Missouri and the Christmas Cruise in 2024.

Last year, 200,000 people attended the Christmas Experience and the cruise was so popular it inspired the series “Christmas at Sea.” This summer, the inaugural Hallmark Stars Live bus tour hosted by 11 year Hallmark Channel fixture Nikki DeLoach, kicked off in New Jersey and wrapped in Nebraska.
Fan Barbara Chartier called the Hallmark Stars Live show she attended in Rhode Island a “true pinch-me moment.”
“There aren’t any Hollywood stars that can hold a candle to the Hallmark stars. They think nothing of making their fans feel special,” she said.
“What you see is what you get. They live and breathe the Hallmark brand. You feel the authenticity,” stated Annie Howell, CCO of Hallmark Media.

In true Hallmark fashion, Chartier met a mother and daughter waiting in line. As fate would have it their seats were near each other. They have kept in touch, and she considers them to be lifelong friends.
For fans, Hallmark programming is a happy diversion from the stresses of daily life.
DeLoach told the crowd in Rhode Island, “Even in our darkest days, when we are in our valleys, we are reaching for the light.”

“It isn’t just a television show. It isn’t just a great performance. It is what people take away. They feel like they’ve changed a little bit because they spent time with the Hallmark brand,” said Michelle Vicary, Head of Programming at Hallmark Media.
Barbara Niven, who received her SAG card from a Hallmark Hall of Fame movie and has worked with Hallmark for 23 years, nearly its entire existence, says the network’s appeal is not surprising.
“In this world that needs positive energy, Hallmark creates that, and I think we remind people that there is good out there, and that people can be good and kind and loving.”

title: Director of Mr. T Documentary Marvels at How the Cultural Icon Became a ‘Superhero’
summary: “Untold Mr. T: I Pity the Fool” director Scott Weintrob speaks with TODAY.com about Mr. T’s rise to fame and what makes him so compelling.
story: Let’s conduct an experiment: Close your eyes and think of the 1980s. In the diorama of your mind, maybe you’re seeing Jordache jeans, Ferris Bueller or Pac-Man. They’re all fine and dandy, but, come on, how could you not think of Mr. T?

Mr. T, born Laurence Tureaud, is the quintessential American success story of the decade, a star who is the subject of the Netflix documentary, “Untold Mr. T: I Pity the Fool,” premiering Sept. 8, which chronicles his improbable rise to fame, while taking viewers back to the peak of his popularity.
“This movie is a nostalgia bomb,” director Scott Weintrob tells TODAY.com.

It is, and it’s so much more, peeling back the layers of how Mr. T actually became Mr. T. One of 12 children, he grew up in a Chicago ghetto. Adorned with a display window’s supply of necklaces around his neck, along with earrings, sunglasses and a shocking mohawk, he burst on the scene opposite Sylvester Stallone as the villainous Clubber Lang in 1982’s “Rocky III.”
The documentary traces his evolution and looks back at a defining moment of his youth when his mother was robbed and he sought retribution.
“Mr. T had a situation that he faced after his mother was attacked that turned him into what we know as Mr. T, their superhero,” Weintrob says.

The documentary also dives into the etymology of his self-given moniker and how fame found him. After the incident with his mother, he became a bodyguard and was eventually cast in “Rocky III,” before landing the part of B.A. Baracus in “The A-Team,” an NBC action series that became a big hit.

Mr. T was a superstar. A cartoon series followed. Stickers. Breakfast cereal. Action figures. Endorsement deals out the yin yang. He got in on the movement to not do drugs. And, of course, there’s the catch phrase. “I pity the fool” was as ubiquitous as his muscles.
“Mr. T was so famous. He had fame that people today just don’t even understand because everybody watched the show,” Weintrob says of “The A-Team.”

It’s easy to dismiss Mr. T as a character from the decade of decadence, but that’s not fair. As the documentary explores, he’s always been interested in raising up the downtrodden. He just happened to blaze a trail for others in the process.
“He did set the standard for so many artists to dress how they wanted to dress, dress loud, be noticed,” Weintrob says.

“Mr. T told me that Muhammad Ali always told him, ‘Stand out. You need to stand out if you want to be noticed.’ And I feel like we live in a generation now of young kids trying to stand out and be noticed … This is a different time, and it was all about being yourself. And he was one of the first.”

“The A-Team” offered Mr. T a chance to change the narrative after his menacing turn in “Rocky III.” He was still enormous and tough, but also human, as evidenced by the recurring bit on the show that addressed his character’s fear of flying. After “The A-Team” came out, he crossed the bridge from terrifying to teddy bear, one of the 1980s most memorable personalities.

“He was the right person at the right time,” Weintrob says. “Remember, when TV was so focused on just a few shows that everybody watched them, when Mr. T walked onto the screen, everybody was like, ‘Who is that?’ We’d never seen anyone quite like him.
“There’s a bravery to that. There’s a bravery to putting yourself out there in a way that people may criticize, and he didn’t care. He was always going to be the person that he believed in.”
There’s a bravery to putting yourself out there in a way that people may criticize, and he didn’t care. He was always going to be the person that he believed in.
Scott Weintrob on Mr. t
Today, you can watch what you want when you want, on any number of platforms, a far cry from how the world worked when “The A-Team” was on. The options were limited, which worked out for Mr. T.

“You were given one or two or three or four clear streams of entertainment, and you watched them when they were on, and that was that. And Mr. T was the champion,” Weintrob says. “There was no one else quite like him at the time, and there’s still no one else quite like him today.”
In an era when audiences were presented with characters — think Alf or Pee-Wee Herman — Mr. T was authentic.
“He was Mr. T onscreen and Mr. T offscreen. He was the same character, and people were just so shocked by it,” Weintrob says.
“Mr. T is an incredible human. There’s only one Mr. T. There’ll never ever be another like him,” he adds.
Singular in nature, Mr. T still elicits a reaction among people, one that Weintrob wants to bring out in “Untold.”

“I hope viewers watch this and come away with it and feel good,” he says. “I hope they feel happy. There’s an emotion that comes with watching the film, and if you don’t feel anything at the end, well, it probably wasn’t the right film for you.”

It’s been more than 40 years since “Rocky III” and the premiere of “The A-Team.” Mr. T remains as beloved today as he ever was. Sure, there’s some nostalgia, but he remains dedicated to uplifting others.

“Going out to dinner with Mr. T is a very lengthy experience because it takes him 25 minutes to get from the door to the table because he talks to everybody. Everybody comes up to him. He loves everybody, and everyone loves him,” Weintrob says.

Mr. T, in an interview with The Guardian published Sept. 3, disavowed the documentary, saying it focused too much on his stereotypical image. “If you don’t know me, you’re gonna think I’m some monster,” the documentary quoted him as saying.

Weintrob, in an interview with TV Insider published Sept. 8, responded to the criticism, saying he had a different takeaway from his film’s subject. He said the last time he saw Mr. T was at a screening: “He loved it. He cried, he hugged us.”
“These words of he doesn’t like it. I don’t even know where they even came from. They sound like untruths,” he said.

“Is it heartbreaking that a journalist says that Mr. T doesn’t like it? Not in the slightest. What is exciting is we’ve made a film that’s brilliant, really exciting about someone that people can be inspired by,” he continued.

title: The Opening Line of Alice Hoffman’s ‘The Witches of Cambridge’ Is Also How It Ends
summary: Alice Hoffman previews the beginning of “The Witches of Cambridge,” her new book which was chosen as a Read With Jenna pick.
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.
Alice Hoffman, author of the “Practical Magic” series, is back with another book about witches, but they’re not the Owens sisters.
“The Witches of Cambridge,” out Sept. 8 and named as Read with Jenna’s September pick, unfolds at a secret society for witches at Radcliffe College in the 1950s.

Ava, unaware of her magical heritage, and Lauren, who is extremely aware of hers, both come to terms with their powers and legacies against the backdrop of the Red Scare. As Joseph McCarthy’s witch hunts play out miles away in Washington, D.C. Lauren and Ava explore the lingering presence of the Salem Witch Trials in their own lives and in Cambridge.
The book opens with an evocative sentence about Ava’s isolated childhood in Maine, where she was raised by parents who wanted to hem her in and deny her magic.
In every story there is a beginning, and this was hers, the one she had been waiting for all her life.
“That’s the way I want my life to open,” Hoffman tells TODAY.com, laughing.

In a way, Hoffman’s life reads like a story. She grew up in a single-parent, working-class household. A self-described “secret writer,” Hoffman never thought she could become an author, and she nearly dropped out of high school. Her older brother, studying in California, encouraged her to attend college. Her writing career unfolded fast while at Stanford: She won a writing award and published her first novel at 21. Since then, she has published 30 books.
Ava’s life also opens when she goes to college.

“Ava going off from Maine to have a different life, she doesn’t really know who she is. She goes off to Cambridge and she’s with people very different than she grew up with. This is the beginning for her,” she says.
Hoffman had a second college experience, one that inspired “The Witches of Cambridge,” when she decided to study at the Harvard Divinity School.

“I was surrounded by younger people with so much kind of hope. It was definitely their beginnings,” she says. “I felt very influenced by being with a lot of young people who were searching and looking to kind of restart their lives.”
“The Witches of Cambridge” follows a four-year college experience, and then some, for Lauren and Ava. But it doesn’t end with an ending. Hoffman says the first line echoes the last line of the book.
All you had to do was begin.
Their lives are cyclical: right when one chapter ends, another begins. Hoffman feels she isn’t done following their story, and is currently at work on a sequel.
“I feel like it could end where it did, but there’s so much more that could happen,” she says.

title: Should Celebrities With Dance Backgrounds Be on ‘DWTS’? Mark Ballas Shares His Thoughts
summary: “Dancing With the Stars” pro Mark Ballas reacts to celebrities with dance backgrounds competing on the show.
story: “Take It From Me” is a TODAY.com series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this latest installment, “Dancing With the Stars” pro Mark Ballas breaks down celebrities with dance backgrounds competing on the show.
Every year after a new “Dancing With the Stars” cast is announced, fans have varying opinions about the latest celebrities vying for the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy — and this year is no different.

Sixteen stars will be competing on Season 35 of the competition show, some with past dance experience. Among them is Julia Stiles, known for her moves in “Save the Last Dance,” and Jenna Dewan and Harry Shum Jr., who are both trained dancers.
Some social media users have been criticizing their casting, arguing that they have an advantage over other celebrities with no prior experience.
But “DWTS” pro Mark Ballas has a different take.

“The show’s called ‘Dancing With the Stars,’ not ‘Dancing With the Stars With No Dance Experience,’” he tells TODAY.com. “Good luck casting 12 to 16 people in the entertainment industry, and one of them hasn’t danced before.”
The 40-year-old dancer and three-time Mirrorball champ also notes that dance experience is not always an advantage.

“It’s about finding teams that you’re invested in. The cool thing about the show is it’s all about preference, right?” he says before mentioning the voting process that determines which couples remain on the show every episode.
The different skill level, he says, is what makes “DWTS” exciting and keeps viewers tuning in.

“If you had a whole show of complete and utter beginners who can’t dance at all, that’s not fun. And if you have it the other way, with all dancers, that’s not as fun either,” Ballas continues. “But it’s fun to see great dances. It’s fun to see people struggle and then overcome the struggle. And it’s fun to see people who are like, ‘Oh wait, how come you’re, like, accidentally pretty good at this?’”
He adds that what’s great about “DWTS” is that “it feeds every different viewer for what they want to see.”
Carrie Ann Inaba, who has been a judge since the first season, also chimed in on the debate. She explained that it matters what previous dance styles a celebrity has tried before being cast.

“What’s difficult — and I don’t think people realize this — is when you go from being a jazz dancer or a hip-hop dancer or all the other forms of dancing (to ballroom),” she told Entertainment Weekly. “The weight placement is so different. It’s weird because your body has memory, so it remembers how to dance, and it thinks it already knows how to do these moves, but it doesn’t.”
She added, “It takes a lot of time to un-train the body to put your weight on the front more over your toes instead of back and down and grounded.”
“It’s not as easy as people think,” Inaba said, pointing out that the advantage some dancers have is based on their rhythm and musicality.

Going into his 22nd season, and this time with fellow “Traitors” alum Maura Higgins as his partner, Ballas tells TODAY.com he just wants his partners to “feel like they got the best experience that they possibly could.”

“It’s a once in a lifetime experience. And think about it, it’s quite silly, we’re ballroom dancing on telly and you get a new style every six days, and you’re just hoping that you make it to the end,” he shares.
The new season of “Dancing With the Stars” premieres Sept. 15, with a second episode on Sept. 16.

title: What Happened in the Elizabeth Holmes Doc, According to Someone Who Saw It
summary: Here’s what the Elizabeth Holmes documentary was like according to a person who was at a screening at Sundance.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
A surprise documentary about Theranos founder and convicted felon Elizabeth Holmes has created instant buzz after a screening at a film festival and the release of a trailer that has gone viral.

Rebecca Keegan of NBC News Digital was in attendance at the Telluride Film Festival in Colorado when the documentary “You Can See Everything” was screened on Sept. 7. The film was directed by absurdist comedian Nathan Fielder and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim and produced jaw-dropping reactions from those in the crowd.
“There were audible gasps and ‘no ways’ consistently throughout this almost three-hour film,” Keegan told NBC News correspondent Erin McLaughlin on TODAY Sept. 8.

Holmes was the founder and CEO of the tech startup Theranos, which promised to revolutionize blood testing. She was found guilty of four counts of wire fraud in January 2022 after a federal investigation uncovered critical violations in a Theranos lab following reports that the technology did not work and could deliver faulty results.

The new documentary, which will be released in October, features footage of Holmes and partner Billy Evans with their two children at a rental home in San Diego before Holmes entered federal prison in 2023. She is scheduled to be released in 2031.
“I think part of the film is exploring this question of Elizabeth Holmes’s perception of reality and about things that she’s done,” Keegan said.
A trailer released by the studio A24 on Sept. 7 shows a wide-eyed Holmes awkwardly only inches away from Fielder’s face as she speaks to him in one scene.

“I’m not that person,” Holmes says in the clip. “I can promise you that. I don’t have anything to deceive you on. Of course, I’m not deceiving you. I’m engaging with you as a human being. Why would I deceive you? There’s no reason for me to do that.”
“OK. All right. OK, good chat,” Fielder replies.
The two then stare at each other for an uncomfortable duration.
“You’re being real right now?” Fielder asks.
“I’m always being real,” Holmes replies.
Keegan described a “strange feeling” produced by the interactions between Fielder and Holmes in the film.
“Fielder is very much a character in the film, and in some ways, it’s him trying to understand whether he believes Elizabeth Holmes or not,” Keegan said.

“I’m struggling to this day to understand exactly what I experienced,” Fielder said during the post-screening Q&A, according to Keegan. “I don’t know why they want me there. I’m a weird guy. I don’t get it. That messed with my head.”

The conversations between Holmes and “The Rehearsal” star are reportedly not the only surreal moments in the documentary. The film also includes an A-list Hollywood actress reenacting Fielder’s conversations with Holmes from prison. Fielder asked the attendees at the screening not to reveal the actress’s identity, according to Keegan.
NBC News reached out to Holmes for comment, but did not hear back. Holmes shared the movie trailer on her X account on Sept. 6 and wrote, “I’m always being real.”

“You Can See Everything” is the latest screen adaptation of the saga involving Holmes. HBO released the documentary “The Inventor” about Holmes in 2019, and then Amanda Seyfried played her in the 2022 Hulu series “The Dropout.”

title: Would Sheinelle Ever Join ‘RHONY’? Jenna Gets Answers About that Rumor
summary: Jenna Bush Hager asked Sheinelle Jones if she would consider joining the cast of Bravo’s “The Real Housewives of New York City.”
story: Sheinelle Jones beams into living rooms every day from New York City on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle, so would she consider adding another iconic New York show to her resume?
On the Sept. 8 episode of the show, Sheinelle and Jenna chatted with the “RHONY” cast, and Jenna mentioned there had a been a rumor that Sheinelle would be one of the housewives on the program.
“By a show of hands, who thinks she should join next season?” Jenna asked, as the entire cast cheered and raised their hands.
“It’s like being in an encouraging classroom,” Sheinelle said.
Jenna then Sheinelle outright: “Would you ever do it?”
“We’re going to keep the suspense,” she said coyly.
“That’s a maybe,” Jenna said.
“There you go,” Sheinelle said.
“You’d be filming all day long,” Jenna said, while Sheinelle asked the cast if cameras were around them 24/7.
“She’s getting some fact finding info,” Jenna said, prompting Sheinelle to laugh.

Sheinelle may not be part of the “Real Housewives” universe, but fans can still check out the 16th season of “RHONY,” which premieres Sept. 8 at 8 p.m. ET on Bravo and streams the next day on Peacock.

The new season will see Season 15 returnees Sai De Silva, Erin Lichy and Jessel Taank joined by Hailey Glassman, Erika Hammond and Daisy Toye. Rounding out the cast is Carole Radziwill, back full-time on the reality show for the first time since 2018’s Season 10.
Radziwill has said her return to the franchise is an “opportunity” after her name appeared in files related the Jeffrey Epstein investigation.

“I mean, I felt like this isn’t something I shy away from,” Radziwill said at a press event Sept. 1. “Me and many, many, many, many more people found their names in these files. And it’s not something I shy away from because I think, really, it’s important to talk about it. It’s important to be transparent. Obviously, I didn’t know anything, as no one, you know, 20 years ago would have known anything.”

title: Sandra Bullock Pries Hoda Kotb for More Details About Her ‘Connection’ With Man on Plane
summary: Sandra Bullock asked Hoda Kotb for more information about he man she met on a plane, sparking talk about a possible love connection.
story: Sandra Bullock turned the tables on Hoda Kotb in order to try and get some intel on her love life.

Hoda sat down with Bullock and Nicole Kidman to discuss their upcoming movie, “Practical Magic 2,” but the “Speed” star wanted to find out more about the mystery man Hoda met on a plane and discussed when she visited TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle on Aug. 21.
Bullock said she saw the segment in which Hoda opened up about the encounter.
“A question was posed to you about a flight that you took, and there was a little conversation and a little sparklet? What happened?” Bullock asked.
“So I was on a plane and I sat next to some guy, and he’s super whatever,” Hoda said.
“Handsome? Super handsome?” Bullock fired back.
Hoda confirmed she and the man swapped phone numbers before they went their separate ways.

“I didn’t know if it was a connection like just a bond for a second, or was it something — I don’t know. I still don’t know,” she said, while Bullock looked at the camera and mouthed the words, “Call her,” promoting Hoda to laugh.
“This is my favorite interview ever,” Hoda howled, as Bullock mouthed “soft skin” while caressing her arm.
“This is intense,” Kidman joked.
“Did you say ‘soft skin’? You are so weird,” Hoda told Bullock.
“Well, that’s important. If you look at someone and you go, ‘Am I going to enjoy touching their very soft skin?’ You will enjoy it,” Bullock replied.

While chatting with Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones last month, Hoda divulged details of what seemed like a meet cute with the mystery man, saying their chat on the plane was “firing on all cylinders.” After the flight, the pair bumped into each other again in Cannes while her company Joy 101 was there, and they said hello to each other. They would later text, but Hoda wasn’t sure where things stood. She did confirm the man was single.
“Look. There are connections,” she said. “I don’t know what it is.”

title: Sandra Bullock Shares How Her Kids Appear in ‘Practical Magic 2’ — and Their Reactions to Surprise Cameo
summary: Sandra Bullock’s two teen children had no idea they are in the upcoming “Practical Magic 2” until she gave them a sweet surprise.
story: Sandra Bullock’s two teen children had no idea they are in the upcoming “Practical Magic 2” until she gave them a sweet surprise.

Bullock adopted son Louis, now 16, in 2010 and daughter Laila, now 13, in 2015. She told Hoda Kotb that “Practical Magic 2” was the first movie set the teens were old enough to remember being on, and the first film in which they actually made the final cut.

Bullock, 62, spoke alongside co-star Nicole Kidman on the Sept. 8 episode of Hoda’s “Making Space” podcast about how her kids were involved in the highly anticipated sequel to the 1998 cult hit, which hits theaters Sept. 10.
She said her kids had several questions about life on set, from “Where are you going?” to “Can we watch?” and finally, “Can we be in it?”
But “every time I put them in the background before, it’s gotten cut,” Bullock said. “Sorry. Show business.”
Things were different with “Practical Magic 2,” though, and Bullock said she put their voices, “their essences,” in the film.

Using “little recordings from when they were babies and then all the way up,” Bullock was finally able to put her kids into one of her films. The teenagers didn’t find out until the film’s premiere in Los Angeles on Aug. 31.
“Last night when it came up, they’re all like, ‘That’s me?’ And they got to see themselves as babies and little toddlers. And yeah, it was very sweet,” she said.
“So they didn’t get cut out,” Bullock added with a laugh. “They’re kinda in it.”
Kidman, 59, is also a parent of teenagers, in addition to two adult children she has with ex-husband Tom Cruise. She shares Sunday Rose, 18, and Faith Margaret, 15, with ex-husband Keith Urban.
Her children were also on the set of “Practical Magic 2.”

“They’ve been on sets pretty much their whole lives,” Kidman told Hoda. “So it was more like they were in London in the summer, and it was just beautiful for them. And my niece was there, and so for us it was just a family kind of affair. And they would come and go and watch things, and both of them have seen this movie now. They hadn’t seen the original.”
She said her teens have since watched the original film in which Bullock and Kidman play the Owens sisters, who are the descendants of witches and learn the use of practical magic while growing up.
The two Oscar winners also tried to prepare Hoda, whose daughters are 9 and 7, for what it will be like when she becomes the mom of teenagers.

“I think it’s a joy,” Kidman said. “I mean, is it hard? Aspects of it can be challenging. But at the same time, is it extraordinary to accompany these people on their journey, on the beginning of their journey, and just say, ‘I’m here. I’m your guide. I’m hopefully your home, your safe place, and the world is your oyster?’”
Bullock described how she approaches parenting differently. While she is white, both of her children are Black.

“I mean, we’re different this, you know?” she said while gesturing to her skin. “I’m uber paranoid, and they will tell you. They’re like, ‘Mom, it’s going to be fine.’ I’m like, ‘It’s not fine. It’s not fine outside.’ The energy that is floating around our country and our world.

“Again, the color of their skin. They’re my babies, they’re my life, but no one knows that when they leave my house,” she continued. “So that is always in the forefront of my mind. But I’m now learning to trust them. Where they are now is extraordinary.”

title: From ‘Traitors’ to Red Carpet Debut, Phaedra Parks and CT Tamburello’s Relationship Timeline
summary: Fans shipped Chris “CT” Tamburello of “Real World” fame and “Real Housewives” alum Phaedra Parks when they appeared on “The Traitors.” Now the pair admitted that they are dating.
story: Chris “CT” Tamburello of “Real World” fame may have won Season 2 of Peacock’s “The Traitors” competition show, but he also began a connection that blossomed long after leaving the Scottish castle: he is in a relationship with fellow contestant Phaedra Parks, a mortician and “Real Housewives” alum.
Yes, that’s right — the chemistry that fans of the show spotted on screen eventually led to a relationship off-screen.
Could “faithful” fans have possibly willed this relationship into existence? We’ll never know ... but we can hope!
So, how did these “traitors” become “faithful” to each other? Here’s a timeline of key moments in Parks and Tamburello’s relationship.
Fall 2023: Parks and Tamburello Meet While Filming ‘The Traitors’
Tamburello, 46, and Parks, 52, film Season 2 of “The Traitors” on location in Scotland.
The second season of the show featured familiar faces — and notable rivals — from popular reality TV programs.

Tamburello made his way to the cast via MTV. He first appeared on “The Real World: Paris” then went on to find success on “The Challenge.” Per People, he has won “The Challenge” five times (plus two spinoff seasons) and competed in 19 seasons.
His “Challenge” rival, Johnny “Bananas” Devenanzio, also competed in this season of “The Traitors.”

The witty and outspoken Parks starred on “The Real Housewives of Atlanta” from 2010 to 2017, as well as in 2025 and 2026. She now dabbles in several projects, and on her Instagram page, she describes herself as an “attorney to the stars,” mommy, mortician, model, actress and author.
On both shows, she sparred for screen time with fellow Atlanta “Housewives” star Shereé Whitfield.
Early 2024: ‘The Traitors’ Premieres — and Fans Watch Their Connection Unfold
Episodes of Season 2 of “The Traitors” aired from January to March 2024.
The vibes between the two were noticeable.

Tamburello may have a tough Boston accent, but he seemed to turn into a softie around Parks. And while Parks could eviscerate an opponent in 30 seconds or less, she seemed surprisingly sweet on Tamburello, calling him her “Castle Daddy.”

Tamburello ultimately helped remove Parks from the castle, but as he voted for her as a Traitor, he smiled and said, “I think you came on here to be the opposite of who you are in real life. And I think you’ve been the best Traitor we’ve seen yet.”
March 2024: These Fan Favorites Comment on Their Chemistry During Press Tour
In an interview that spring, Vulture flat out told Parks, “So the internet wants you and CT to be boyfriend and girlfriend.”
Parks replied, “Oh, god.”

She went on to say, “CT is a great guy, and we definitely had a wonderful connection. He’s a sweetheart. He’s a really good guy, and he’s attractive and all those good things. He’s a gentleman. There was never anything romantic between us at all. It was just a sweet, pure friendship.”
Tamburello shared similar sentiments in an interview with Entertainment Weekly in March 2024.

“No, nothing real happened, I’ll be honest with you,” he said in the interview. “It was fun. I loved her because she’s a cornball. She was great. I would say there was a sense of sincerity, for sure. But it was also playing a game, you know?”
August 2026: Parks Admits She Might Have More Than a Friendship With Tamburello
During a Sept. 4 appearance on “Jeff Lewis Live,” Parks said that she would be attending the Emmys with a date that was “not” platonic.
Admittedly wanting to make a splash with their relationship, Parks withholds details but shared that something has been brewing with a mysterious “CT” for a while.
A caller piped up to “connect the dots” for everyone.

“They were on ‘The Traitors’ together. She called him her ‘castle daddy’ on the show,” said a caller identified only as Megan. “So I know you want to wait to disclose it to the world, but please don’t plead the fifth. Let us know if it’s that CT.”
“Ummmm ... I think so,” Parks replied hesitantly.
Lewis confirmed that he could see Tamburello outside the studio, and that the “CT” Parks mentioned was definitely her “Traitors” competitor.
September 2026: Tamburello and Parks Hard Launch Relationship on the Red Carpet
Phaedra Parks doesn’t do anything halfway, and the hard launch of her relationship with Tamburello is no exception.
The pair stunned on the red carpet at the first night of the 78th Emmy Awards in Los Angeles on Sept. 5.

Along with photos from the evening, Parks posted this comment on her Instagram page on Sept. 6: “Some came for the awards. I came with the prize. Thank you to the real trophy for making a beautiful night even better.”
Fellow “Traitors” contestant and occasional “Challenge” rival Devenanzio used the same comment and hilariously paired it on Instagram with photos of him and Tamburello from the same event.
Parks posted a response: “We are a thropple.”

title: ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Teases James and Oliver Phelps As New Castle Keepers
summary: A first look at James and Oliver Phelps, known as Fred and George Weasley in “Harry Potter” films, as Alan Cumming’s castle keepers in “The Traitors: New Blood.”
story: “The Traitors” is gearing up for its first season filled with “every day Americans” — and it appears host Alan Cumming is getting help from some famous twins.
TODAY has an exclusive first look at the new castle keepers in “The Traitors: New Blood,” James and Oliver Phelps.

Best known for playing Fred and George Weasley in the “Harry Potter” films, the actors will keep an eye on Cumming’s castle as he welcomes the new recruits and puts them through the ultimate game of deceit.
The clip, shared Sept. 7, begins with a glimpse at the reality show’s famous Scottish castle before a phone rings and one of the Phelps brothers answers.
“Keeper, is the castle set?” Cumming is heard asking, with one brother replying, “It is, Alan” while the other also makes an appearance and adds, “Oh, it is Alan.”
The brothers then raise the castle flag as Cumming says, “Let the games begin.”

While the U.S. version of “The Traitors” has only featured celebrities over its four seasons, “New Blood” will welcome 22 civilians into the Scottish Highlands castle. The cast along with their mischievous portraits were revealed on Aug. 12.

Once there, the game is the same with the contestants either chosen as a Traitor or Faithful. Determined to win the $250,000 prize, the Faithfuls will then seek out the Traitors and attempt to not get eliminated (aka “murdered”), while the Traitors try to deceit the Faithfuls and not get banished from the castle. As for James and Oliver Phelps, the actors will be on hand to help the competition be as treacherous as ever.
“The Traitors: New Blood” premieres Sept. 17 on NBC at 8 p.m. with back-to-back episodes. They will be available to stream the next day on Peacock.
New episodes will air every Thursday at the same time on the network.
(Peacock and NBC are owned by NBCUniversal, TODAY’s parent company).

title: Oasis Frontmen and Brothers Liam Gallagher and Noel Gallagher Reunite on Red Carpet Following Feud
summary: The Gallagher brothers, Liam and Noel, made a rare appearance on the red carpet on Sept. 5 at the Venice International Film Festival screening of “Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger.”
story: British band members and brothers Noel Gallagher, 59, and Liam Gallagher, 53, are responsible for megahits like “Wonderwall,” “Champagne Supernova” and the titular “Don’t Look Back in Anger.” Despite their success, the band split more than a decade ago due to the all-too-frequent feuds.

The Gallagher brothers made a rare appearance on the red carpet on Sept. 5 at the Venice International Film Festival screening of “Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger,” a new documentary about the behind-the-scenes drama surrounding their highly anticipated 41-date reunion tour in 2025.
The documentary opens in theaters on Sept. 11.
Could the tour have brought the brothers closer together? Perhaps. They certainly seemed at ease on the Venice red carpet, smiling, hugging, pulling faces and even holding hands in a victory pose.
Noel Gallagher even got playful and stuck his tongue out at the photographers during the red carpet.
Oasis had been broken up since August 2009 following a reported brawl between the two. Noel Gallagher then announced he was quitting the band after a show at a festival in Paris.
While the two had pursued their own solo careers, they announced their reunion tour in August 2024.
This is not the first time post-breakup that the brothers seem to have found a new rhythm together.
Last August, Noel Gallagher told the British radio show talkSPORT that his brother Liam Gallagher has been “amazing” and “smashing it.”
That was quite a turnaround for the brothers, who frequently sparred on social media and in interviews over the years.
“I guess when it’s all said and done, we’ll sit and reflect on it, but it’s great being back in a band with Liam,” Noel Gallagher said in the interview. “I forgot how funny he was.”
He continued, “Liam’s smashing it, and I’m proud of him.”

Noel Gallagher, who had been working as a solo artist alongside his band the High Flying Birds following Oasis’ breakup, added about his brother, “I’ve got to say, I kind of look at him and think, ‘Good for you, mate.’ He’s been amazing.”

title: Behind Raygun’s ‘Cringe’ Olympic Breakdancing Routine Is An Oddly Sweet Love Story
summary: Australian breakdancer Rachael Gunn — who’s better known under her stage name Raygun — competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics, becoming the center of ridicule. But husband Samuel Free stuck by her side.
story: When Australian breakdancer Rachael Gunn — who’s better known under her stage name Raygun — competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics, she became the focus of memes, ridicule and a deluge of parodies.
But one person wasn’t laughing. In fact, unlike pretty much all of social media at the time, he found her moves rather breathtaking.

Samuel Free, Gunn’s husband and coach, is among the key figures featured in the new Netflix documentary “Untold Raygun: Breaking Badly,” which chronicles the events around the viral routine that set social media aflame.

The documentary, which was released Sept. 1, includes voices from other dancers who were less-than-impressed by Gunn’s breakdancing skills. But Free stands fiercely by Gunn’s moves, which included some, uh, odd choices like the sprinkler and a pose meant to mimic a kangaroo. He goes so far as to say that he was captivated by her routine.
“I was struck by the beauty of her performance,” Free says in the documentary of her Olympics appearance.
Free’s comments in the documentary have prompted social media users to describe the two as a match made in heaven, with some even hoping to find the same level of devotion in a partner.
“May all of us have partners as supportive as Raygun‘s husband was at the Olympics,” one social media user wrote on Threads.

Raygun went viral after her two performances in Paris did not earn a single point from the judges across four rounds. There, she lost by a combined 36-0 to two competitors. And her moves elicited everything from memes to Halloween costumes.
How Did Raygun Meet Her Husband, Samuel Free?
Raygun’s connection to the sport actually goes back to Free, who is responsible for introducing her to breakdancing, the documentary shows.
Free, a breakdancer himself, once competed under the name Sammy Sex. He says in the doc that he became drawn to the art form at an early age when he watched the 1984 film “Breakin.’”
“They’re doing big moves,” Free says. “I didn’t even know people could do this!”

He says he kept up with breakdancing through the years, which ended up being a “sticking point” in many of his romantic relationships throughout his 20s — that is, until he met Gunn while working at a call center.
“I have a life-changing moment,” Free recalls of meeting Gunn. “I remember walking past this girl in the break room.”

The two ended up hitting it off, according to the film. Gunn, who was in college at the time, says that Free “opened up my world.” For Gunn, one particularly pivotal moment was when he took her to a breaking battle, she says.
“Walking into this space felt like I walked into a movie,” Gunn says in the documentary.
It was after that battle, during which she was inspired by one of the women dancers, that she decided that she wanted to pursue breakdancing. And right by her side was Free.

“Sammy was my cheer squad, my fan, my biggest supporter,” Gunn, a university lecturer whose research revolved around breaking as well, says in the film. “He’s special ... makes you feel like you can do things when you’re around him.”
Free, who eventually started to coach her, says that they began “building a life together.” And in 2018, the two got married.
“Our wedding was so beautiful,” Gunn says over footage from their big day, which appeared to include quite a bit of craziness on the dance floor. “We were just so happy.”
How Did Free Help His Wife Prepare For The Olympics?
The two speak in the film about their experience preparing for the Olympics after Gunn had qualified to represent Oceania. They say that Gunn hit the gym and Free pushed her to train hard.
“I was like, ‘As your husband, I am in awe of how hard you’re working. Props to you. As your coach, you need to work harder. This is not clean,’” Free recounts.

In the lead-up to Paris, the couple says that they realized it was unlikely she’d best any of the other competitors. So instead of focusing on power moves — like windmills and headspins, for example — they decided to take a different approach. Free suggested they shift the routine into an ode to Australia, helping her incorporate moves reminiscent of swimming and the now-infamous kangaroo freeze, they recount.
While in Paris, some others were weary of what Gunn had planned to do, Free was stoked.
“This is Rachael’s moment. It’s her saying, ‘I’m doing me,’” Free says.
What Did Raygun’s Husband Think Of The Aftermath Of The Performance?

The aftermath of Gunn’s performance was pretty ugly, the documentary shows. And Free says that the onslaught of memes, trolling and bullying from the internet was a “massive trauma.” At the time conspiracies spread that Free was on the committee that had chosen Gunn to represent their country in the Olympics — something that’s been shot down by organizers, other competitors and the couple themselves. Still, the two spent a few months in the Netherlands in an attempt to lie low and recover from the incident.
It’s been a while since the 2024 Paris games, and Gunn admits that she was “cringe.”
“I brought shame and embarrassment on the country,” she says.
However, she underscores that she’s still dancing and that “Paris hasn’t defeated me.” As for Free, he’s still standing right by her side.
He says that his wife’s “performance connected with people, whether that’s genuine excitement and entertainment or outrage.”
“It generated discourse and got the entire world talking,” he says.

title: After ‘Ted Lasso’ Feature, Negro Leagues Baseball Museum ‘Can Hardly Handle’ Surge In Visitors, Its President Says
summary: The Negro Leagues Baseball Museum, which preserves the long history of African American baseball in the U.S., was featured in the premiere of the new season of “Ted Lasso” in August. And it’s been flooded with visitors ever since.
story: Kansas City, Missouri’s Negro Leagues Baseball Museum is now dealing with a good problem to have.

The historical institution, which preserves the long history of African American baseball in the U.S., was featured in the premiere of the new season of “Ted Lasso” in August. And since, the museum’s president Bob Kendrick tells TODAY.com, the establishment has been flooded with visitors. Sales, Kendrick says, are up around 50% to 60% compared to where they were last year at this time.

“I’ll tell you — it has superseded anything that I could have ever even remotely imagined,” Kendrick says of the outpouring of interest in the museum from the show. “I honestly did not know that it would have this kind of interest and immediate impact on the museum.”

While the show’s third season, which wrapped in May 2023, ended with star and co-creator Jason Sudeikis’ character Ted Lasso leaving his life in the UK for Kansas City, the new season is all about his hop back across the pond. This time, Ted is tasked with helping to lead AFC Richmond women’s soccer team, the Lady Greyhounds, to success.

But the first episode of the new season doesn’t start in the UK. Ted, who’s now working in a grocery store and parenting his son, still needs some convincing to leave the stability behind for the coaching gig abroad. And several of his old friends, including Rebecca, Keeley and Higgins, show up in KC to do just that.

While there, Higgins, played by Jeremy Swift, attempts to hit up the American Jazz Museum — which is housed in the same building as the NLBM — but finds it unexpectedly closed for the day. So he ends up taking a tour of the baseball establishment and becomes wildly moved by the figures he’s introduced to. One of these impactful players is the legendary Satchel Paige, widely recognized as one of the best pitchers in the history of the game. Paige’s career in the Negro Leagues began the 1920s.

“Satchel was a showman. He had a wild throwing style and all these crazy names for his pitches. ‘The Hesitation.’ The Midnight Creeper.’ ‘The Dipsy-Do’,” an NLBM employee, played by actor Milan Carter, tells Higgins. “Many thought old Satch would be the first to break the major league color barrier. He wasn’t. But he finally got in at the age of 42. Oldest rookie in history, and he was still incredible.”
As the NLBM staff member says in the show, “the Negro Leagues were glorious.”

“They didn’t do it for fame or fortune. They did it ‘cause to not play would have been unacceptable,” the staff member says of the leagues, which were formed in 1920 as a response to a decades-long unwritten “gentleman’s agreement” between club owners that kept Black players out of all professional leagues with white players.

The visit leaves a huge impression on Higgins, who is seen later in the episode, decked out in a Kansas City Monarchs jersey. The Monarchs were one of the most successful teams in the Negro Leagues and boasted Paige as one of its alumni.
Kendrick tells TODAY.com that the episode’s representation of the museum was moving.

“The scene was so beautifully done,” Kendrick says. “The care, the concern, the understanding of the essence of what Negro Leagues history represented both on and off the field —you saw that in that scene.”
The only complaint he’s gotten?

“I got a lot of calls, people ask me why wasn’t I in it. Because they wanted me to be the guy that was talking about Satchel Paige,” he says, before laughing. “What I told him was, ‘Number one, you never play yourself. You go find somebody who’s younger and better looking for you.’”
Kendrick explains that the NLBM scenes were filmed about a year ago. Back then, he says he had no idea what would happen after the episode aired.

“Perhaps I was a little bit naive on just how big this show really is,” he says. “It has just absolutely captivated the hearts and the imaginations of ‘Lasso’ fans around the world, and it obviously has exposed Negro League’s history and this museum to millions of people around the globe.”
Kendrick, who met Sudeikis years ago at a holiday ceremony, says that the “Ted Lasso” creator has visited the museum and been a fan for some time.
